78245.e: In 1492 Columbus sailed west with three ships and reached the Caribbean. The “egg of Columbus” stands for an amazingly simple solution.
78245.m: Columbus reached America in 1492, although he was looking for India.

78246.q: Which expedition do these emojis show?
a: First passage through the Northwest Passage
78246.e: The expedition led by Ferdinand Magellan set off in 1519 and returned to Spain in 1522. Magellan was killed on the way in the Philippines, and Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the voyage.
78246.m: Magellan's expedition proved that you can sail round the Earth.

78247.q: Which seafarer do these pictures mean?
78247.e: Vasco da Gama sailed round Africa and reached Calicut in India in 1498. This allowed Portugal to buy spices directly by sea.
78247.m: Vasco da Gama opened the sea route to Indian spices for Portugal.

78248.q: Which traveller from Venice is meant?
78248.e: In the 13th century Marco Polo travelled to the court of the Mongol ruler Kublai Khan in China. His travel account “Il Milione” aroused great interest in Asia in Europe.
78248.m: Marco Polo's travel account shaped Europe's image of China for a long time.

78249.q: Which polar explorer do these pictures mean?
78249.e: The Norwegian Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911. He relied on dog sleds; Scott arrived about a month later.
78249.m: Amundsen won the race to the South Pole with dog sleds.

78250.q: Which event of 1953 do these emojis show?
a: Climb of the Eiger north face
78250.e: On 29 May 1953 Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first people to stand on the highest mountain in the world. Everest is about 8849 metres high.
78250.m: In 1953 Hillary and Tenzing were the first to reach the summit of Everest.

78251.q: Which seafarer mapped the east coast of this continent in 1770?
78251.e: In 1770 the Briton James Cook sailed along the east coast of Australia and landed at Botany Bay. There his crew described the kangaroo for Europe for the first time.
78251.m: James Cook was the first to map the east coast of Australia.

78252.q: Which historical process do these emojis show?
78252.e: After 1492 plants such as maize, potatoes, tomatoes and cocoa came from America to Europe. In return, wheat, horses and cattle came to America.
78252.m: Many of Europe's staple foods today come from America.

78253.q: Which event of 14 July 1789 do these emojis show?
78253.e: On 14 July 1789 citizens of Paris captured the Bastille prison, a symbol of royal power. The day is now France's national holiday.
78253.m: In France, 14 July commemorates the beginning of the Revolution.

78254.q: Which event of 1773 do these emojis show?
78254.e: In 1773 colonists threw chests of tea into Boston harbour to protest against British taxes. Their motto was “No taxation without representation”.
78254.m: The Boston Tea Party was a protest against taxes without a say.

78255.q: Which period of upheaval do these emojis show?
78255.e: From about 1760 in England, machines and factories increasingly replaced handwork, first in textile production. Towns grew quickly.
78255.m: Industrialisation began in the English textile industry.

78256.q: Which document of 4 July 1776 do these emojis show?
78256.e: The declaration drafted by Thomas Jefferson separated the thirteen colonies from Great Britain. The 4th of July is still celebrated with fireworks today.
78256.m: On the 4th of July the USA celebrates its independence.

78257.q: Which peaceful revolution of 1989 do these emojis show?
78257.e: In Czechoslovakia demonstrators jingled keys to ring in the end of the communist government. The writer and playwright Václav Havel became president at the end of 1989.
78257.m: The Velvet Revolution was largely non-violent.

78258.q: Which protests of 1989 do these pictures mean?
78258.e: After prayers for peace in St Nicholas Church, from September 1989 more and more people marched through Leipzig with candles every Monday. Their chant was “We are the people”.
78258.m: The Leipzig Monday demonstrations remained peaceful.

78259.q: Which change in the New Stone Age do these emojis show?
78259.e: From about 10,000 BC people in the Fertile Crescent began to grow grain and keep animals. They settled down and later also made pottery vessels.
78259.m: With farming, people settled in one place.

78260.q: Which upheaval in England in 1688/89 do these emojis show?
78260.e: William III of Orange and Mary II took the English throne together. The Bill of Rights of 1689 strengthened the power of Parliament.
78260.m: The Glorious Revolution strengthened the English Parliament.

78261.q: Which peace treaty of 1919 is meant?
78261.e: The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles. It ended the First World War with Germany.
78261.m: The peace treaty was signed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles in 1919.

78262.q: Which organisation of the interwar period do these emojis show?
78262.e: The League of Nations began its work in 1920 and had its seat in Geneva, the city with the Jet d'Eau. It was meant to prevent wars through negotiation.
78262.m: Geneva was the seat of the League of Nations.

78263.q: Which event in the first winter of the war do these emojis show?
78263.e: At Christmas 1914 soldiers on the Western Front spontaneously took a break, sang songs and exchanged presents. In some places they even played football.
78263.m: The Christmas Truce of 1914 arose spontaneously among the soldiers.

78264.q: Which Swiss measure in the Second World War do these emojis show?
78264.e: With the Wahlen Plan from 1940, Switzerland wanted to produce more of its own food. Even parks and sports grounds in towns were planted with potatoes and grain.
78264.m: Friedrich Traugott Wahlen planned Switzerland's Cultivation Battle.

78265.q: Which organisation, founded in 1945, do these emojis show?
78265.e: The United Nations was founded in 1945 after the Second World War to secure world peace. Its headquarters are in New York.
78265.m: The UN is meant to promote peace and cooperation between countries.

78266.q: Which achievement at Bletchley Park is meant?
78266.e: During the Second World War British experts around the mathematician Alan Turing cracked the Enigma cipher machine. Their work also contributed to the development of early computers.
78266.m: Alan Turing helped to decipher the Enigma codes.

78267.q: Which person do these emojis show?
78267.e: From 1942 to 1944 the Jewish girl hid with her family in a secret annexe in Amsterdam and wrote a diary. From the window she could see a chestnut tree.
78267.m: The Diary of Anne Frank is one of the best-known books about the Nazi era.

78268.q: Which resistance group do these emojis show?
78268.e: In 1942 and 1943 students in Munich around Hans and Sophie Scholl distributed leaflets against the Nazi regime. The group called itself the White Rose.
78268.m: The White Rose resisted National Socialism with leaflets.

78269.q: Which event of 9 November 1989 do these emojis show?
78269.e: During the night of 9 to 10 November 1989 the border crossings in Berlin opened. People celebrated on the Wall and began to chip pieces out of it.
78269.m: 9 November 1989 stands for the fall of the Berlin Wall.

78270.q: Which relief operation of 1948/49 do these emojis show?
78270.e: During the blockade of West Berlin, Western aircraft supplied the city from the air for almost a year. Pilots dropped sweets on little parachutes for children.
78270.m: In Berlin the airlift planes were called raisin bombers.

78271.q: Which crisis of 1962 do these emojis show?
78271.e: In October 1962 the USA and the Soviet Union came close to nuclear war over Soviet missiles in Cuba. A naval blockade and negotiations ended the crisis, after which a direct telephone line was set up.
78271.m: After the Cuban Missile Crisis, Washington and Moscow set up a hotline.

78272.q: Which rapprochement of 1971 do these emojis show?
78272.e: In 1971 the US table tennis team visited China, which paved the way for President Nixon's visit in 1972. Sport opened a diplomatic door.
78272.m: A table tennis tournament helped bring the USA and China closer together.

78273.q: Which reform movement of 1968 do these emojis show?
78273.e: Under Alexander Dubček, Czechoslovakia wanted to create “socialism with a human face”. Warsaw Pact troops ended the reforms in August 1968.
78273.m: The Prague Spring was an attempt to make socialism freer.

78274.q: Which slogans of Soviet reform policy from 1985 do these emojis show?
78274.e: Mikhail Gorbachev relied on glasnost, meaning openness and transparency, and perestroika, the restructuring of the economy and state. The reforms changed the Eastern Bloc fundamentally.
78274.m: Gorbachev stood for openness and restructuring in the Soviet Union.

78275.q: Which gesture of 1970 do these emojis show?
78275.e: In 1970 West German Chancellor Willy Brandt knelt before the memorial to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto. The gesture became a symbol of his policy of reconciliation with the East.
78275.m: Willy Brandt's kneeling became a symbol of reconciliation.

78276.q: Which alliance founded in 1949 has a symbol that looks like these emojis?
78276.e: NATO's symbol is a four-pointed compass star in a circle. The alliance was founded by Western countries in Washington in 1949.
78276.m: NATO was founded in 1949 as a Western defence alliance.

78277.q: Which mission of 1969 do these emojis show?
78277.e: On 20 July 1969 Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon. Michael Collins stayed in orbit in the command module.
78277.m: In 1969 Neil Armstrong was the first person to set foot on the Moon.

78278.e: On 4 October 1957 the Soviet Union launched the beeping metal sphere Sputnik 1 into space. It was the first artificial Earth satellite and caused the “Sputnik shock” in the USA.
78278.m: Sputnik 1 was the Earth's first artificial satellite.

78279.q: Which animal was the first living creature to orbit the Earth, in 1957?
78279.e: In November 1957 the dog Laika flew into Earth orbit on board Sputnik 2. There was no plan for her to return.
78279.m: Laika was the first living creature in Earth orbit.

78280.q: Which space traveller do these pictures mean?
78280.e: On 12 April 1961 Yuri Gagarin became the first person to orbit the Earth, in Vostok 1. The flight lasted about 108 minutes.
78280.m: In 1961 Yuri Gagarin was the first person in space.

78281.q: Which female space traveller do these emojis show?
78281.e: In June 1963 the Soviet citizen Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space, in Vostok 6. She orbited the Earth for almost three days.
78281.m: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space.

78282.q: Which space traveller do these pictures mean?
78282.e: In 1992 Claude Nicollier from the canton of Vaud became the first Swiss person in space. Altogether he took part in four Space Shuttle missions.
78282.m: Claude Nicollier is the first Swiss astronaut.

78283.q: Which instrument in space do these emojis show?
78283.e: The Hubble telescope was launched in 1990 but had a wrongly ground mirror. In 1993 a Shuttle mission gave it corrective optics, a kind of pair of glasses.
78283.m: The Hubble telescope got a kind of pair of glasses in space.

78284.q: Which facility in space do these emojis show?
78284.e: Since 1998 the ISS has been run jointly by the USA, Russia, Europe, Japan and Canada. People have lived there permanently since 2000.
78284.m: People have lived on the ISS without a break since 2000.

78285.q: Which message to aliens do these emojis show?
78285.e: Since 1977 each of the two Voyager probes has carried a gold-plated record with pictures, music and greetings in many languages. Voyager 1 is now the most distant human-made object from Earth.
78285.m: The Voyager probes carry a golden record with greetings from humanity.

78287.q: Which person from Swiss history do these emojis show?
78287.e: Niklaus von Flüe lived as a hermit in the Ranft in Obwalden and was valued as an adviser. His advice helped the Confederates reach agreement in the Covenant of Stans in 1481.
78287.m: Brother Klaus is regarded as the peacemaker of the old Swiss Confederacy.

78288.q: Which event of 1529 do these emojis show?
78288.e: In the First War of Kappel, Catholic and Protestant troops are said to have eaten a milk soup together at the border. There was no battle, and a peace was agreed.
78288.m: The Kappel milk soup is a symbol of reconciliation in Switzerland.

78289.q: Which construction of 1882 do these emojis show?
78289.e: The summit tunnel, about 15 kilometres long, was built from 1872 under the direction of Louis Favre, and the breakthrough came in 1880. The railway opened in 1882 and linked northern and southern Europe.
78289.m: The Gotthard Railway was a milestone in Swiss transport history.

78290.q: Which person from Geneva do these emojis show?
78290.e: In 1863 Henry Dunant inspired the founding of the International Committee of the Red Cross. In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.
78290.m: Henry Dunant is regarded as the founder of the Red Cross.

78291.q: Which document of 1848 created the modern Swiss federal state?
78291.e: The Federal Constitution of 12 September 1848 turned the confederation of states into a federal state. Among other things it created the Federal Council and the two-chamber parliament.
78291.m: Switzerland has been a federal state since 1848.

78292.q: Which Geneva festival do these emojis show?
78292.e: The Escalade commemorates the defeat of Savoy's night attack on Geneva in December 1602. Today families smash a chocolate pot, the “marmite”.
78292.m: At the Escalade in Geneva a chocolate pot is smashed.

78293.q: Which principle of Swiss foreign policy, recognised internationally in 1815, do these emojis show?
78293.e: At the Congress of Vienna and in the Treaty of Paris of 1815 the great powers recognised Switzerland's permanent neutrality. Since then Switzerland has committed itself not to take part in other countries' wars.
78293.m: Swiss neutrality was recognised internationally in 1815.

78294.q: Which change of 1971 in Switzerland do these emojis show?
a: Election of the Federal Council by the people
78294.e: On 7 February 1971 the men accepted the federal right for women to vote and be elected. Appenzell Innerrhoden only had to introduce it at cantonal level in 1990.
78294.m: Since 1971 women in Switzerland have been able to vote and be elected at federal level.

78295.q: Which form of direct democracy do these emojis show?
78295.e: At the Landsgemeinde, voters gather in the open air and vote by raising their hands. Today it still exists in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
78295.m: The Landsgemeinde is one of the oldest forms of democracy.

78296.q: Which people's right in Switzerland lets you demand a vote on a law passed by parliament?
78296.e: With 50,000 signatures within 100 days of publication, the people can vote on a new federal law. Eight cantons can also call for a referendum.

78297.q: Which principle of the state do these emojis show?
78297.e: State power is divided between the legislature, the executive and the judiciary so that they keep each other in check. Montesquieu described the principle in 1748.
78297.m: Three separate branches of power protect against abuse of power.

78298.q: Which term from Swiss politics is meant?
78298.e: From 1959 to 2003 the seven Federal Council seats were always shared out in the ratio 2:2:2:1 between the FDP, CVP, SP and SVP. This fixed distribution is called the magic formula.
78298.m: For a long time the magic formula decided the make-up of the Federal Council.

78299.q: Which voting principle do these emojis show?
78299.e: In Switzerland a change to the constitution needs a majority of voters and a majority of the cantons. This is called the popular majority and the cantonal majority.
78299.m: In Switzerland, changes to the constitution need both the people and the cantons.

78300.q: Which procedure of Athenian democracy do these emojis show?
78300.e: Citizens scratched the name of a politician on a piece of pottery, an ostrakon. Whoever got the most votes had to leave Athens for ten years.
78300.m: In ostracism the Athenians voted with pieces of pottery.

78301.q: Which document of 1948 do these emojis show?
78301.e: The UN General Assembly adopted the declaration in Paris on 10 December 1948. In 30 articles it sets out rights that belong to all people.

78302.q: Which inventor do these pictures mean?
78302.e: Around 1450 Johannes Gutenberg developed printing with movable metal type in Mainz. This meant books could be made much faster and more cheaply.
78302.m: Gutenberg's printing press changed the way knowledge spread.

78303.q: Which invention, made practical for everyday use by Thomas Edison in 1879, do these emojis show?
78303.e: In 1879 Edison developed a long-lasting light bulb with a carbon filament. He then also built power stations and electricity networks for lighting.
78303.m: Edison made the light bulb practical for everyday use.

78304.q: Which inventor is behind this picture puzzle?
78304.e: Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone in the USA in 1876. His surname is the English word for the bell in the picture.
78304.m: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.

78305.q: Which machine do these emojis show?
78305.e: Fire heats water, and the steam drives pistons and wheels. Thomas Newcomen built one of the first usable steam engines in 1712.

78306.q: Which Swiss development of 1875 do these emojis show?
78306.e: In 1875 Daniel Peter from Vevey managed to make a chocolate with milk that kept well. Milk chocolate became one of Switzerland's export hits.
78306.m: Daniel Peter developed a long-lasting milk chocolate in Vevey.

78307.q: Which invention, credited to Cai Lun around AD 105, do these emojis show?
78307.e: Around AD 105 the Chinese official Cai Lun described how to make paper from plant fibres such as tree bark and hemp. The fibres were dissolved in water and scooped out with a sieve.

78308.q: Which Swiss invention do these emojis show?
78308.e: After a walk, the engineer George de Mestral from Vaud saw burrs in his dog's fur and studied them under a microscope. From this he developed a fastening system with tiny hooks and loops.
78308.m: Velcro is an example of an invention modelled on nature.

78309.q: Which discovery of 1928 do these emojis show?
78309.e: Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould in a Petri dish killed bacteria. This led to the first widely used antibiotic.
78309.m: Penicillin was the first widely used antibiotic.

78310.q: Which crisis, which began on the New York Stock Exchange in 1929, do these emojis show?
78310.e: The stock market crash in October 1929 set off a worldwide depression with mass unemployment. Switzerland also suffered badly from it in the 1930s.
78310.m: The Great Depression began with a stock market crash in 1929.

78311.q: Which speculative bubble of the 17th century do these emojis show?
78311.e: In the Netherlands, huge prices were paid for single tulip bulbs for a while. In February 1637 the market suddenly collapsed.
78311.m: Tulip mania is regarded as one of the first speculative bubbles.

78312.q: Which crisis of 1973 do these emojis show?
78312.e: In 1973 the Arab oil-producing countries cut oil production, and the price of oil rose sharply. Because of this, Switzerland had car-free Sundays in the autumn of 1973.
78312.m: The oil crisis showed how dependent the economy is on oil.

78313.q: Which stock market bubble burst around the year 2000, as these emojis show?
78313.e: In the late 1990s the shares of young internet companies rose sharply. From March 2000 the bubble burst, and many companies went bankrupt.

78314.q: Which reconstruction programme for Europe from 1948 do these emojis show?
78314.e: After the Second World War the USA supported the rebuilding of Western Europe with loans and aid. The programme was named after Secretary of State George C. Marshall.
78314.m: The Marshall Plan helped rebuild Western Europe.

78315.q: Which programme of President Franklin D. Roosevelt do these emojis show?
78315.e: From 1933 Roosevelt fought the economic crisis with state building projects, social insurance and banking reforms. Millions of unemployed people found work again.
78315.m: The New Deal was the USA's answer to the great crisis.

78316.q: Which historical trade route do these emojis show?
78316.e: Along this network of caravan routes, silk, spices and porcelain travelled from China to the Mediterranean. The name was coined by the geographer Ferdinand von Richthofen in 1877.
78316.m: Goods and ideas were exchanged between East and West along the Silk Road.

78317.q: In which ancient kingdom, according to the common view, were the first coins minted?
78317.e: In the 7th century BC Lydia in Asia Minor minted coins of electrum with a lion's head. The Lydian king Croesus became proverbial for his wealth.
78317.m: The first coins come from Lydia in Asia Minor.

78318.q: Which crisis in the Swiss watch industry do these emojis show?
78318.e: In the 1970s cheap quartz watches, mainly from Japan, conquered the world market. Many mechanical watchmakers in Switzerland had to close or merge.
78318.m: The quartz crisis hit the Swiss watch industry hard in the 1970s.

78319.q: Which event of 1 January 2002 do these emojis show?
78319.e: On 1 January 2002 euro coins and banknotes came into circulation in twelve countries. The euro had already existed as non-cash money since 1999.
78319.m: Since 2002 people in many European countries have paid with euro cash.

78320.q: Which agreement do these emojis show?
78320.e: The agreement was signed in 1985 in the wine village of Schengen in Luxembourg and provided for the removal of passport checks at internal borders. Switzerland has applied it since 2008.
78320.m: In the Schengen Area there are no systematic border checks.

78321.q: Which European community of 1951 do these emojis show?
78321.e: In 1951 France, Germany, Italy and the Benelux countries pooled their coal and steel production. This community is regarded as the seed of today's EU.
78321.m: The European Coal and Steel Community joined the coal and steel of six countries.

78322.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78322.e: The melody from the last movement of Beethoven's 9th Symphony is the European anthem. The Council of Europe chose it in 1972, and the EU adopted it in 1985.
78322.m: The European anthem comes from Beethoven's 9th Symphony.

78323.q: Which symbol do these emojis stand for?
78323.e: The flag shows twelve golden stars in a circle on a blue background. The number twelve stands for perfection, not for the number of member states.
78323.m: The flag of Europe always has twelve stars.

78324.q: Which Swiss referendum of 1992 do these emojis show?
78324.e: On 6 December 1992 the people and the cantons narrowly rejected joining the European Economic Area. After that, Switzerland relied on bilateral agreements with the EU.
78324.m: In 1992 Switzerland said no to the European Economic Area.

78325.q: Which award of 2012 do these emojis show?
a: Nobel Peace Prize for the EU
78325.e: In 2012 the European Union received the Nobel Peace Prize. It was honoured for its contribution to peace, reconciliation and democracy in Europe.
78325.m: The EU was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012.

78326.q: Which event do these emojis show?
78326.e: In June 2016 a majority in the United Kingdom voted to leave the EU. At the end of January 2020 the country left the Union.
78326.m: The United Kingdom left the EU in 2020.

78327.q: Which event of 1517 do these emojis show?
78327.e: In 1517 Martin Luther published 95 theses against the sale of indulgences in Wittenberg. Whether he really nailed them to the church door is disputed.
78327.m: Luther's 95 Theses changed the Church in Europe.

78328.q: Which term from physics do these pictures make together?
78328.e: Electricity (lightning) and a magnet together make an electromagnet. A coil with current flowing through it produces a magnetic field that can be switched on and off.
78328.m: An electromagnet only works while current is flowing.

78329.q: Which force of nature do these pictures show?
78329.e: The falling apple and the Earth stand for gravity. According to legend, a falling apple gave Isaac Newton the idea for his law of gravitation.
78329.m: Gravity makes all masses attract each other.

78330.q: Which optical phenomenon do these pictures show?
78330.e: White light is split into the colours of the rainbow by a prism (triangle). This is called dispersion, because refraction depends on the wavelength.
78330.m: In dispersion, white light is split into its spectral colours.

78331.q: Which term from physics do these pictures mean?
78331.e: A loudspeaker and a wave together make a sound wave. Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium such as air.
78331.m: Sound waves cannot travel through a vacuum.

78332.q: Which physical effect do these pictures mean?
78332.e: When an ambulance drives past, the siren sounds higher as it approaches and lower as it moves away. Christian Doppler described this Doppler effect in 1842.
78332.m: In the Doppler effect the pitch changes when the source is moving.

78333.q: Which famous thought experiment do these pictures show?
78333.e: A cat, a box and a radioactive substance belong to Schrödinger's cat. In 1935 Erwin Schrödinger used it to illustrate the strange superposition states of quantum mechanics.
78333.m: Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment in quantum mechanics.

78334.q: Which law of physics do these pictures show?
78334.e: According to legend, Archimedes used the water displaced in his bath to test whether a crown was pure gold. Archimedes' principle says that the buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced liquid.
78334.m: Buoyancy equals the weight of the displaced liquid.

78335.q: Which optical phenomenon do these pictures show?
78335.e: Light hits a mirror and is sent back. This is reflection; the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
78335.m: In reflection the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

78336.q: Which thought experiment from the theory of relativity do these pictures show?
78336.e: One twin travels in a rocket at nearly the speed of light and ages more slowly than his brother on Earth. The reason is the time dilation of special relativity.
78336.m: According to relativity, fast-moving clocks run more slowly.

78337.q: Which chemical formula goes with this picture?
78337.e: The salt shaker stands for table salt. Table salt is sodium chloride with the formula NaCl.
78337.m: Table salt is made of sodium and chlorine.

78338.q: Which chemical process do these pictures show?
78338.e: Electric current splits water into the gases hydrogen and oxygen. This process is called electrolysis.
78338.m: In electrolysis, electric current splits a compound.

78339.q: Which acid do these pictures make together?
78339.e: An ant and a test tube make formic acid, from the Latin “formica” for ant. It used to be obtained from ants and, with the formula HCOOH, is the simplest carboxylic acid.
78339.m: Formic acid is the simplest carboxylic acid.

78340.q: Which chemical process do these pictures mean?
78340.e: Iron reacts with water and oxygen to form brown rust. This destruction of metals by chemical reactions is called corrosion.
78340.m: Rust is a form of corrosion of iron.

78341.q: Which change of state do these pictures mean?
78341.e: Ice turns directly into gas without becoming liquid first. This change from the solid to the gaseous state is called sublimation.
78341.m: In sublimation a solid becomes a gas directly.

78342.q: Which element symbol goes with this picture?
78342.e: The silver medal stands for silver. Its symbol Ag comes from the Latin word argentum.
78342.m: The element symbol of silver is Ag.

78343.q: Which chemical element do these pictures mean?
78343.e: The balloon gas that makes your voice sound high like a mouse is helium. Sound travels faster in light helium, so the tone of the voice shifts upwards.
78343.m: Helium is lighter than air and a noble gas.

78344.q: Which substance do these pictures mean?
78344.e: A toothbrush, a tooth and a shield stand for fluoride in toothpaste. Fluoride hardens tooth enamel and protects against tooth decay.
78344.m: Fluoride in toothpaste protects teeth from decay.

78345.q: Which laboratory aid do these pictures mean?
78345.e: A strip of paper that turns red or blue is litmus paper. It turns red in acids and blue in alkalis.
78345.m: Litmus paper turns red in acids and blue in alkalis.

78346.q: Which animal behaviour do these pictures mean?
78346.e: In autumn, birds fly to warmer parts of the world. This behaviour is called bird migration; swallows from Switzerland, for example, spend the winter in Africa.
78346.m: Migratory birds spend the winter in warmer regions.

78347.q: Which biological process do these pictures mean?
78347.e: Over time, bacteria turn milk sugar into lactic acid. This lactic acid fermentation produces yoghurt and soured milk.
78347.m: Yoghurt is made by lactic acid fermentation.

78348.q: Which technical term do these pictures mean?
78348.e: The caterpillar turns into a butterfly via the pupa. This profound transformation is called metamorphosis.
78348.m: In metamorphosis an animal completely changes its shape.

78349.q: Which biological theory do these pictures show?
78349.e: The development from ape-like ancestors to humans stands for evolution. Charles Darwin founded the theory of evolution in 1859 with his book on the origin of species.
78349.m: Humans and great apes have common ancestors.

78350.q: Which phenomenon from biology do these pictures mean?
78350.e: The harmless hoverfly looks like a bee or wasp that can sting, and so is putting on an act. This imitation of a dangerous animal to scare off enemies is called mimicry.
78350.m: In mimicry a harmless animal imitates a well-defended one.

78351.q: Which form of living together do these pictures show?
78351.e: The bee gets nectar and the flower is pollinated: both benefit. Living together like this to the advantage of both is called symbiosis.

78352.q: Which ability of living things do these pictures show?
78352.e: A lizard can shed its tail and then partly grow it back. The ability to replace lost body parts is called regeneration.

78353.q: Which ability of animals do these pictures mean?
78353.e: Bats give out ultrasonic calls and listen to the echo. With echolocation they can find their way even in complete darkness.
78353.m: Bats find their way using ultrasound.

78354.q: Which astronomical term do these pictures mean?
78354.e: The pictures show the Moon from new moon to full moon. These changing shapes of light are called the phases of the Moon; a whole cycle takes about 29.5 days.
78354.m: A lunar cycle from new moon to new moon lasts about 29.5 days.

78355.q: Which sight in the sky do these pictures mean?
78355.e: When the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, its shadow falls on the Moon. During this total lunar eclipse the Moon glows reddish, and people call it a blood moon.
78355.m: During a blood moon the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.

78356.q: Which view of the universe do these pictures mean?
78356.e: The Sun is at the centre, and the Earth goes round it. This is the heliocentric model, which Nicolaus Copernicus published in 1543.
78356.m: In the heliocentric model the Sun is at the centre.

78357.q: Which event in space do these pictures show?
78357.e: A star that explodes is a supernova. For a short time it shines as brightly as a whole galaxy.
78357.m: A supernova is the explosion of a star.

78358.q: Which unit of length in astronomy do these pictures mean?
78358.e: Light, a year and a ruler make the light year. It is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.
78358.m: A light year is a distance, not a measure of time.

78359.q: Which type of star do these pictures mean?
78359.e: A red, swollen star is a red giant. Our Sun will also reach this stage in about 5 billion years.
78359.m: One day our Sun will become a red giant.

78360.q: Which sight in the sky do these pictures mean?
78360.e: A small piece of rock from space burns up in the Earth's atmosphere and appears as a shooting star. This streak of light is called a meteor; if a piece reaches the ground, it is called a meteorite.
78360.m: A meteor is the trail of light of a piece of rock burning up.

78361.q: Which event do these pictures mean?
78361.e: An explosion from which the universe and time emerge stands for the Big Bang. According to today's measurements it happened about 13.8 billion years ago.
78361.m: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old.

78362.q: Which medical term do these pictures mean?
78362.e: Blood and the letters A and B stand for the blood groups of the ABO system. Karl Landsteiner discovered them in 1901.
78362.m: Karl Landsteiner discovered the blood groups.

78363.q: Which examination do these pictures mean?
78363.e: A heart, electric voltage and a curve stand for the electrocardiogram, or ECG for short. It records the electrical activity of the heart.
78363.m: An ECG measures the electrical activity of the heart.

78364.q: Which examination do these pictures mean?
78364.e: A brain, electric voltage and a curve stand for the electroencephalogram, or EEG for short. It measures brain waves through electrodes on the scalp.

78365.q: Which imaging technique do these pictures mean?
78365.e: A strong magnet that takes pictures of the inside of the body stands for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). It works without X-rays and shows soft tissue such as the brain in great detail.
78365.m: MRI works with magnetic fields instead of X-rays.

78366.q: Which medical emergency do these pictures mean?
78366.e: If the blood supply in the brain is cut off, nerve cells die. This is a stroke, where every minute until treatment counts.
78366.m: In a stroke every minute counts.

78367.q: Which injury do these pictures mean?
78367.e: A bone that breaks and needs treatment stands for a fracture. This is the medical term for a broken bone.
78367.m: Fracture is the technical term for a broken bone.

78368.q: Which disease do these pictures mean?
78368.e: Blood sugar that is too high is the sign of diabetes mellitus. It is caused by a lack of insulin or by insulin working less well.
78368.m: In diabetes the blood sugar is too high all the time.

78369.q: Which examination do these pictures mean?
78369.e: Lungs, breath and measuring stand for spirometry. It measures how much air someone can breathe in and out.
78369.m: Spirometry measures how well the lungs work.

78370.q: Which term from computing do these pictures mean?
78370.e: A beetle, or bug, in the computer stands for a program error. Finding and fixing such errors is called debugging.
78370.m: When debugging, you look for errors in a program.

78371.q: Which kind of malware do these pictures mean?
78371.e: Like the wooden horse of the Greeks at Troy, a Trojan disguises itself as a harmless gift. Once installed, it gives attackers access to the computer.
78371.m: A Trojan disguises itself as a useful program.

78372.q: Which internet scam do these pictures mean?
78372.e: Fake emails are used to fish for passwords. The name of this scam is based on the English word fishing.
78372.m: Genuine companies never ask for passwords by email.

78373.q: Which term from computing do these pictures mean?
78373.e: The picture shows a biscuit, which Americans call a cookie. A cookie is a small file that a website saves in the browser, for example for settings.
78373.m: Cookies store a website's data in the browser.

78374.q: Which term from computing do these pictures mean?
78374.e: A message is protected with a key and numbers. With encryption, only authorised people with the right key can read the content.
78374.m: Encryption protects data from prying eyes.

78375.q: Which number system do these pictures mean?
78375.e: A number system with only the digits 0 and 1 is the binary system. Computers store all data in this form as bits.
78375.m: Computers calculate in the binary system with 0 and 1.

78393.e: A dinosaur in rock stands for a fossil. Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from earlier ages of the Earth, turned to stone.
78393.m: Fossils are evidence of life from prehistoric times.

78405.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
78405.e: Wind turns a wheel, and this makes electricity. Wind turbines turn the movement energy of the air into electrical energy.
78405.m: Wind turbines use the movement energy of the air.

78428.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78428.e: The maple leaf is on Canada's flag, the beaver is an official national symbol and ice hockey is the national winter sport. Together, that makes Canada.
78428.m: Canada is the second largest country on Earth by area.

78429.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78429.e: Koalas live in the wild only in Australia, and almost all kangaroos live there too. The dry outback covers large parts of the country.
78429.m: Australia is both a country and a whole continent.

78430.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78430.e: Tacos, cacti and the colourful piñata are seen as typical of Mexico. Maize for tortillas was grown there thousands of years ago.
78430.m: Mexico is the Spanish-speaking country with the most people in the world.

78431.e: The picture shows Mount Fuji, the highest mountain in Japan, along with sushi and the Shinkansen high-speed train, which has been running since 1964.
78431.m: Mount Fuji is a volcano and, at 3776 metres, the highest mountain in Japan.

78432.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78432.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in China; chopsticks and red lanterns, for example at the Lantern Festival, are part of Chinese culture.
78432.m: China is one of the countries with the most people on Earth.

78433.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78433.e: Elephants, curries and yoga, which has its origins in India, together point to India.

78434.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78434.e: Camels in the desert, the pyramids and the crocodiles in the Nile point to Egypt.
78434.m: Egypt lies in north-east Africa on the Nile.

78437.q: Which city do these emojis mean?
78437.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of Bern, the Federal Palace is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament, and in clear weather you can see the Alps. Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.
78437.m: Officially, Switzerland has no capital; Bern is the federal city.

78438.q: Which capital do these pictures show?
78438.e: The gate stands for the Brandenburg Gate, the bear for the city's coat of arms and the wall for the Berlin Wall, which divided the city from 1961 to 1989.
78438.m: The Wall divided Berlin into East and West for 28 years.

78440.q: Which capital do these emojis show?
78440.e: The stadium stands for the Colosseum, the fountain for the Trevi Fountain, pasta and scooters for Italian city life. Together that makes the Italian capital.
78440.m: The Colosseum is the largest amphitheatre of the ancient world.

78441.e: The guards outside Buckingham Palace, the red double-decker buses and the frequent rain are seen as typical of London.
78441.m: London lies on the Thames and is the capital of the United Kingdom.

78445.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78445.e: The statue holds a torch and a tablet with the date of the Declaration of Independence. France gave it to the USA, and it was unveiled in New York in 1886.
78445.m: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the USA.

78471.q: Which form of trade do these emojis show?
78471.e: The arrows in a circle show that a cow is swapped directly for grain, without any money at all.
78471.m: In barter, goods are swapped for each other without money.

78473.e: The goods leave your own country and go out into the world. Selling goods abroad is called exporting.
78473.m: Exports are goods that are sold abroad.

78511.e: The ticket divided by two makes half the price. With the Half Fare Travelcard, you travel on Swiss public transport at half price.
78511.m: With the Half Fare Travelcard, you pay only half price on public transport.

78515.e: Red plus sea makes the Red Sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, which is known for its colourful coral reefs and fish.
78515.m: The Red Sea is famous for its coral reefs.

78517.q: Which sea do these emojis show?
78517.e: Olives, lemons and lots of sun typically grow and thrive around the Mediterranean Sea, which separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
78517.m: Around the Mediterranean, there is a warm climate with dry summers.

78519.q: Which natural phenomenon do these emojis show?
78519.e: The pull of the Moon makes the sea level rise and fall regularly. This change between low tide and high tide is called the tides.
78519.m: Low and high tide are caused mainly by the pull of the Moon.

78520.q: Which climate zone do these emojis show?
78520.e: Palm trees, lots of rain and high temperatures all year round mark the tropics around the equator.
78520.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

78521.e: Penguins, snow and the polar night lasting for months mark the coldest areas of the Earth at the poles.
78521.m: In the polar zone, there is the polar night in winter.

78525.q: Which climate zone do these pictures mean?
78525.e: Autumn, spring, summer and winter show the four clear seasons. They mark the temperate zone, where Switzerland lies too.
78525.m: Switzerland lies in the temperate climate zone.

78527.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78527.e: Sand, dromedaries, cacti and strong sun mark the desert. So little rain falls there that hardly any plants grow.
78527.m: Very little rain falls in the desert.

78573.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78573.e: The computer receives a radio signal and needs no network cable. A wireless local network is called Wi-Fi or WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network).
78573.m: Wi-Fi connects devices to the network without cables.

78585.q: Which kind of picture do these emojis show?
78585.e: A painter looks in the mirror and paints himself. A picture like this is called a self-portrait; those by Rembrandt, for example, are famous.
78585.m: In a self-portrait, artists show themselves.

78588.q: Which art technique do these emojis mean?
78588.e: Lots of small coloured squares together make a picture. In a mosaic, you put small stones or pieces of glass together to make a picture.
78588.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small coloured stones.

78589.q: Which painting technique goes with these emojis?
78589.e: Painting is done on paper with water, a brush and paint. Painting with see-through water-based paints is called watercolour (in German “Aquarell”, from Latin aqua, water).
78589.m: A watercolour is painted with water-based paints.

78605.q: Which tennis term do these emojis show?
78605.e: When a set reaches 6 games all, a special deciding game is usually played. This game is called a tiebreak.
78605.m: A tiebreak decides a set at 6 games all.

78606.q: Which running event do these pictures mean?
78606.e: The number 42 stands for the distance of 42.195 kilometres. This long-distance race is called a marathon, named after the Greek town of Marathon.

78607.q: Which sport do these emojis show?
78607.e: Swimming, cycling and running are done straight after each other. This endurance sport is called triathlon (Greek tri, three).
78607.m: The triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

78608.q: Which winter sport do these pictures stand for?
78608.e: Skiing and a target stand for the combination of cross-country skiing and shooting. This winter sport is called biathlon (Greek bi, two).
78608.m: Biathlon combines cross-country skiing with shooting at targets.

78609.e: A ball lies about 11 metres in front of the goal, and only the goalkeeper may try to stop it. This kick is called a penalty.
78609.m: A penalty is taken from the penalty spot.

78613.q: Which linguistic term do these emojis show?
78613.e: Hot and cold are opposites. A word with the opposite meaning is called an antonym.
78613.m: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning.

78614.q: Which figure of speech do these pictures stand for?
78614.e: The cat says “miaow”, and the word imitates the sound. This sound painting is called onomatopoeia.

78615.q: Which figure of speech do these emojis show?
78615.e: The sun smiles and waves like a person. When things or natural phenomena are given human qualities, this is called personification.
78615.m: In personification, things are given human qualities.

78616.e: In the telling, a tiny ant turns into a gigantic dinosaur, so something is greatly exaggerated. Strong exaggeration is called hyperbole.
78616.m: A hyperbole is a strong exaggeration.

78617.q: Which figure of speech do these pictures show when you name them in English?
78617.e: Bee, banana and bread all begin with the same sound B. The same initial sound in words that follow each other is called alliteration.
78617.m: In alliteration, words begin with the same sound.

78618.q: Which figure of speech do these emojis stand for?
78618.e: In rainy weather someone says grumpily “Great weather!”. When you say the opposite of what you mean, that is irony.
78618.m: Irony means the opposite of what is said.

78619.q: Which word borrowed from French do these emojis stand for?
78619.e: From a trip to Paris you bring a small keepsake home in your suitcase. The French word souvenir means “memory”.
78619.m: A souvenir is a keepsake from a trip.

78620.q: Which Latin expression fits these pictures?
78620.e: A document goes into the folder and into the archive, the matter is closed. To put something “ad acta” literally means “to the files”, so to regard it as finished.
78620.m: If you put something ad acta, you regard the matter as finished.

78622.q: Which job with a French name goes with these emojis?
78622.e: A person with a cap drives other people in a car. Someone who drives a vehicle as a job is called a chauffeur.
78622.m: A chauffeur drives other people in a car.

78623.q: Which job with a French name is meant?
78623.e: Hair is cut with scissors, and the striped sign stands for a salon. In Switzerland, a hairdresser is called a coiffeur.
78623.m: The coiffeur cuts and styles hair.

78624.q: Which word borrowed from French fits these pictures?
78624.e: A wrong step leads to an embarrassing moment. Faux pas means “false step” in French and refers to a breach of good manners.
78624.m: A faux pas is an embarrassing breach of good manners.

78625.q: Which word borrowed from French is meant?
78625.e: Two people meet with a rose at a set time at a set place. Such an arranged meeting is called a rendezvous.
78625.m: A rendezvous is an arranged meeting.

78626.q: Which loanword from the art world fits these emojis?
78626.e: An exhibition of paintings opens its doors with a party. The festive opening of an art exhibition is called a vernissage.
78626.m: The vernissage is the opening of an exhibition.

78628.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
a: Renoir’s “Bal du moulin de la Galette”
78628.e: In 1888 in Arles, Vincent van Gogh painted several pictures of sunflowers in a vase, all in bright yellow.
78628.m: Van Gogh painted his sunflowers in a vase and almost only in shades of yellow.

78629.q: Which famous painting do these pictures stand for?
78629.e: Van Gogh’s “Starry Night” (1889) shows a swirling night sky with stars and the moon above a village with a church tower.
78629.m: The swirling spirals in the sky make Van Gogh’s “Starry Night” unmistakable.

78630.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78630.e: In 1893 Edvard Munch painted a desperate figure on a bridge under a glowing orange-red sky above the Oslofjord.
78630.m: Munch’s “The Scream” is seen as a symbol of the anxiety of modern people.

78631.q: Which painting do these emojis mean?
78631.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted the woman with the mysterious smile in front of a wide landscape; the picture hangs today in the Louvre in Paris.
78631.m: The Mona Lisa's smile is seen as the most famous in the history of art.

78632.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78632.e: Around 1665, Jan Vermeer painted a girl with a blue and yellow turban and a large pearl at her ear; the shell stands for the pearl.
78632.m: Vermeer’s girl wears a blue and yellow turban and a large pearl.

78633.q: Which work of art do these pictures stand for?
78633.e: Around 1830, Katsushika Hokusai created a woodblock print with a huge wave threatening boats and Mount Fuji in the background.
78633.m: Hokusai’s “Great Wave” is the best-known Japanese woodblock print.

78634.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
78634.e: In 1931 Salvador Dalí painted soft, melting pocket watches in a bare coastal landscape; ants are crawling on one watch.
78634.m: Dalí’s melting clocks are among the best-known images of the 20th century.

78635.q: Which painting do these emojis stand for?
78635.e: In 1964 René Magritte painted a man in a bowler hat and suit whose face is hidden by a floating green apple, in front of a cloudy sky.
78635.m: Magritte hid the face of his man in a bowler hat behind an apple.

78636.q: Which painting do these emojis show?
a: “A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte”
78636.e: In 1942 Edward Hopper painted lonely customers at night in a brightly lit diner behind a large pane of glass.
78636.m: Hopper’s “Nighthawks” shows loneliness in the big city at night.

78637.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78637.e: The free-standing bell tower of Pisa Cathedral was built from 1173 and already began to lean during construction; the pizza stands for Italy.
78637.m: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral.

78638.q: Which structure do these emojis stand for?
78638.e: The covered wooden bridge in Lucerne has triangular painted panels in its gables; in 1993 most of it burned down and it was then rebuilt.
78638.m: Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge is considered the oldest surviving medieval wooden bridge in Europe.

78639.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78639.e: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had the white marble tomb built on the Yamuna river in Agra for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal.
78639.m: The Taj Mahal is a white marble tomb and a symbol of love.

78640.q: Which site do these emojis show?
78640.e: The Incas built the city around 1450 high in the Andes of Peru; in 1911 an expedition led by Hiram Bingham made it world-famous. The llama stands for the Andes.
78640.m: Machu Picchu is an Inca city high in the Andes of Peru.

78641.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78641.e: The fountain in Lake Geneva shoots water about 140 metres into the air and is the landmark of Geneva.
78641.m: The Jet d’eau is the landmark of Geneva.

78642.q: Which building do these emojis show?
78642.e: The Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens was dedicated to the goddess Athena, whose animal and plant are the owl and the olive tree.
78642.m: The Parthenon on the Acropolis was the temple of the goddess Athena.

78643.q: Which building do these emojis stand for?
78643.e: The round fortress above Schaffhausen was built from 1564 to 1589; vines grow on its slope, and every evening at 9 pm the Munot watchwoman rings the little Munot bell.
78643.m: The Munot is the round fortress of Schaffhausen.

78644.q: Which building do these emojis show?
78644.e: Cologne Cathedral with its two tall towers was built from 1248 to 1880, with long breaks, so over 632 years.
78644.m: Building Cologne Cathedral took over 600 years.

78645.q: Which structure do these emojis show?
78645.e: The 285-metre-high dam in Valais holds back the Lac des Dix; it is the highest gravity dam in the world and the tallest structure in Switzerland.
78645.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

78646.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78646.e: Antonio Vivaldi wrote four violin concertos that portray spring, summer, autumn and winter in music.
78646.m: Vivaldi’s “Four Seasons” are four violin concertos.

78647.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78647.e: In 1717 George Frideric Handel had his “Water Music” played on boats on the Thames for King George I.
78647.m: Handel’s “Water Music” was played in 1717 during the king’s boat trip on the Thames.

78648.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
a: “In the Hall of the Mountain King”
78648.e: Edvard Grieg wrote the piece for Ibsen’s “Peer Gynt”: Peer ends up among the trolls of the Mountain King, and the music gets faster and louder.
78648.m: In Grieg’s “Hall of the Mountain King” the music keeps getting faster and louder.

78649.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78649.e: In his suite of 1886, Camille Saint-Saëns portrays lions, elephants, tortoises, kangaroos and other animals in music.
78649.m: In “The Carnival of the Animals” every animal has its own music.

78650.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78650.e: In Sergei Prokofiev’s musical fairy tale (1936) each character stands for an instrument: Peter, the wolf, the duck, the bird and the cat.
78650.m: In “Peter and the Wolf” you get to know the instruments of the orchestra.

78651.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78651.e: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov wrote “Flight of the Bumblebee” for his opera “The Tale of Tsar Saltan” (1900); the racing runs of the violin imitate the buzzing.
78651.m: Rimsky-Korsakov’s “Flight of the Bumblebee” imitates a bumblebee’s buzzing with racing notes.

78652.q: Which piece of music do these emojis stand for?
78652.e: In Maurice Ravel’s “Boléro” (1928) the snare drum plays the same rhythm throughout the whole piece, while the music gets louder and louder.
78652.m: Ravel’s “Boléro” repeats one rhythm and keeps getting louder.

78653.q: Which piece of music do these emojis show?
78653.e: The four opening notes of Beethoven’s 5th Symphony are often interpreted as “Thus fate knocks at the door”; hence the name Symphony of Fate.
78653.m: Beethoven’s Fifth begins with four famous notes like a knock at the door.

78654.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78654.e: In Mozart’s opera (1791) magic instruments help; the bird catcher Papageno appears, and Tamino flees from a serpent and searches for Princess Pamina.
78654.m: Mozart’s “Magic Flute” tells of the bird catcher Papageno and Prince Tamino.

78655.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78655.e: Georges Bizet’s opera (1875) is set in Seville, the city of oranges; Carmen dances, throws a flower and falls in love with a bullfighter.
78655.m: Bizet’s “Carmen” is set in Seville and contains the famous Toreador Song.

78656.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78656.e: Giuseppe Verdi’s opera (1871) is set in ancient Egypt; the Ethiopian princess Aida lives as a captive, and the Triumphal March with trumpets is famous.
78656.m: Verdi’s “Aida” is set in ancient Egypt and is known for its Triumphal March.

78657.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78657.e: In Giacomo Puccini’s opera, the Chinese princess Turandot sets every suitor three riddles.
78657.m: Princess Turandot sets her suitors three riddles.

78658.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78658.e: In Puccini’s opera (1904) the Japanese woman Cio-Cio-San, called Butterfly, waits in Nagasaki for her American naval officer to return.
78658.m: “Madama Butterfly” is set in Nagasaki and tells of a sad love story.

78659.q: Which operatic work do these emojis show?
78659.e: Richard Wagner’s four-part work begins with three Rhinemaidens guarding the Rhinegold, from which a ring is forged; at the end there is a great fire that destroys the world.
78659.m: Wagner’s “Ring of the Nibelung” consists of four operas.

78660.q: Which opera do these emojis stand for?
78660.e: In Wagner’s opera a knight arrives in a boat drawn by a swan; he marries Elsa (Bridal Chorus), but she must never ask his name.
78660.m: In Wagner’s opera, Lohengrin is the mysterious Swan Knight.

78661.q: Which opera do these emojis show?
78661.e: In Wagner’s opera (1843) a cursed captain must sail the seas for ever with his ghost ship.
78661.m: The Flying Dutchman is a captain who sails the seas without rest.

78662.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78662.e: In the musical with the songs of ABBA, Sophie invites three men to her wedding on a Greek island, because one of them could be her father. It premiered in London in 1999.
78662.m: “Mamma Mia!” tells a story with the songs of ABBA.

78663.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78663.e: Andrew Lloyd Webber’s “Cats” is set on a full-moon night in a scrapyard where the cats gather; it is based on poems by T. S. Eliot.
78663.m: In “Cats” the cats meet at night in a scrapyard.

78664.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78664.e: A masked musician lives beneath the Paris Opera, plays the organ and rows his singer Christine across an underground lake full of candles.
78664.m: The Phantom of the Opera wears a mask and lives beneath the Paris opera house.

78665.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78665.e: “Wicked” tells the story of the green-skinned witch Elphaba from the Land of Oz, who flies on a broomstick and travels to the Emerald City.
78665.m: “Wicked” tells the story of the witches of Oz before the famous tale.

78666.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78666.e: Jean Valjean was in a prison camp for stealing bread, is given silver candlesticks by the bishop and later takes care of the girl Cosette.
78666.m: “Les Misérables” is based on the novel by Victor Hugo.

78667.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78667.e: The nanny Mary Poppins arrives with the east wind, flying on her umbrella, pulls everything out of her bag and sings about a spoonful of sugar.
78667.m: Mary Poppins floats through the air with her umbrella.

78668.q: Which musical do these emojis stand for?
78668.e: Near Salzburg, young Maria becomes the governess of the seven von Trapp children and teaches them to sing with her guitar.
78668.m: “The Sound of Music” tells of Maria and the von Trapp family.

78669.q: Which musical do these emojis show?
78669.e: In “Starlight Express” the performers race each other on roller skates as locomotives and carriages; it has been running in Bochum since 1988.
78669.m: In “Starlight Express” the performers move on roller skates.

78670.q: Which group of artists do these emojis stand for?
78670.e: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner and other architecture students founded the Expressionist group “Die Brücke” (The Bridge) in Dresden in 1905.
78670.m: The artists’ group “Die Brücke” was founded in Dresden in 1905.

78671.q: Which art movement do these emojis show?
78671.e: Futurism, proclaimed by Filippo Tommaso Marinetti in 1909, celebrated speed, machines and modern technology.
78671.m: Futurism was fascinated by speed and machines.

78672.q: Which art movement do these emojis stand for?
78672.e: Art Nouveau around 1900 loved curving lines modelled on plants, flowers and peacocks.
78672.m: Art Nouveau decorates with curving plant shapes.

78673.q: Which art movement do these emojis show?
78673.e: Dada began in 1916 at the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich; the name sounds like baby talk and means hobby horse in French, and collages and sound poems are typical.
78673.m: Dada was founded in Zurich in 1916.

78674.q: Which art movement do these emojis stand for?
78674.e: Andy Warhol painted soup cans, Roy Lichtenstein enlarged comic pictures with speech bubbles; both stand for Pop Art.
78674.m: Pop Art turned everyday objects and comics into art.

78675.q: Which period of art do these emojis show?
78675.e: Renaissance means rebirth: antiquity was rediscovered, and artists used the newly studied central perspective.
78675.m: In the Renaissance the art of antiquity was reborn.

78676.q: Which period of art do these emojis stand for?
78676.e: Rococo is named after rocaille, a shell-shaped ornament; playful curves and delicate pastel colours are typical.
78676.m: Rococo takes its name from a shell ornament.

78677.q: Which group of artists do these emojis show?
78677.e: Wassily Kandinsky and Franz Marc founded the group “Der Blaue Reiter” (The Blue Rider) in Munich in 1911; Marc often painted blue horses.
78677.m: Franz Marc and Wassily Kandinsky founded the Blue Rider.

78678.q: Which architectural style do these emojis stand for?
78678.e: Gothic cathedrals rise high with pointed arches and have huge coloured stained-glass windows.
78678.m: Gothic architecture built tall churches with pointed arches and colourful stained glass.

78679.q: Which school of architecture and design do these emojis show?
78679.e: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919; the name is made of the German words for building and house, and basic shapes and primary colours are typical.
78679.m: The Bauhaus combined art, craft and architecture.

78680.q: Which architect do these emojis stand for?
78680.e: Le Corbusier from La Chaux-de-Fonds developed the Modulor system of measurement based on the human body and appeared on the Swiss ten-franc note of the 8th series.
78680.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds and invented the Modulor.

78681.q: Which architect do these emojis stand for?
78681.e: Gaudí’s basilica Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882; his colourful mosaic lizard is in Park Güell.
78681.m: Gaudí’s Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been a building site for over a hundred years.

78682.q: Which artist and architect do these emojis stand for?
78682.e: Hundred and water make Hundertwasser (German hundert and Wasser); his houses are colourful and crooked, with trees planted on the roofs and in the windows.
78682.m: Hundertwasser loved colourful façades and trees on the roofs.

78683.q: Which order of columns do these emojis stand for?
78683.e: The Ionic capital has two spiral volutes that look like ram’s horns.
78683.m: You can recognise Ionic columns by the rolled spirals on the capital.

78684.q: Which order of columns do these emojis show?
78684.e: According to Vitruvius, the Corinthian capital was inspired by a basket around which acanthus leaves grew; hence its rings of leaves.
78684.m: Corinthian columns have a capital of acanthus leaves.

78685.q: Which structure do these emojis stand for?
78685.e: In 1989 the architect I. M. Pei built the glass pyramid as the entrance to the Louvre art museum in Paris.
78685.m: The glass pyramid is the entrance to the Louvre in Paris.

78686.q: Which typeface do these emojis stand for?
78686.e: Helvetica was designed in Switzerland in 1957; its name comes from the Latin Helvetia for Switzerland.
78686.m: Helvetica is a world-famous typeface from Switzerland.

78687.q: Which design object do these emojis show?
78687.e: Hans Hilfiker designed the Swiss railway clock in 1944; later the red second hand shaped like a signal paddle was added.
78687.m: The Swiss railway clock has a red second hand like a signal paddle.

78688.q: Which design classic do these emojis stand for?
78688.e: Hans Coray designed the aluminium chair with a perforated seat for the Swiss National Exhibition of 1939, the Landi.
78688.m: The aluminium Landi chair was designed for the 1939 National Exhibition.

78689.q: Which design classic do these emojis show?
78689.e: Verner Panton designed the first chair made from a single piece of plastic, curved in an S shape and often red.
78689.m: The Panton Chair is made from a single piece of plastic.

78690.q: Which art and design movement do these emojis stand for?
78690.e: From 1917, Piet Mondrian and the De Stijl group worked only with straight black lines, white and the primary colours red, blue and yellow.
78690.m: De Stijl limited itself to straight lines and primary colours.

78691.q: Which design principle do these emojis show?
78691.e: The spiral of a snail shell is often linked to the golden ratio, a ratio of about 1 to 1.618 that is seen as especially harmonious.
78691.m: The golden ratio is seen as an especially harmonious proportion.

78692.q: Which colour relationship do these emojis stand for?
78692.e: Red and green, and blue and orange, lie opposite each other on the colour wheel and intensify each other.
78692.m: Complementary colours lie opposite each other on the colour wheel.

78693.q: Which typography term do these emojis show?
78693.e: Serifs are the small feet at the ends of letters, as in Times New Roman.
78693.m: Serifs are the small feet on letters.

78694.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78694.e: Prince Hamlet of the Danish castle of Elsinore ponders life in the soliloquy “To be or not to be” and holds the skull of the jester Yorick in the graveyard.
78694.m: Shakespeare’s Hamlet asks the famous question “To be or not to be”.

78695.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78695.e: In the famous balcony scene Romeo speaks at night beneath Juliet’s window; the rose recalls her line about names.
78695.m: The balcony scene is the most famous scene from “Romeo and Juliet”.

78696.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78696.e: In Shakespeare’s comedy, fairies play tricks in the woods at night; a craftsman is given a donkey’s head, and Titania, under a spell, falls in love with him.
78696.m: In “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” fairies enchant people in the woods at night.

78697.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78697.e: In Lessing’s drama (1779) the wise Nathan tells the parable of the three identical rings and pleads for tolerance between religions.
78697.m: Lessing’s ring parable pleads for tolerance between religions.

78698.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78698.e: In Goethe’s drama the scholar Faust makes a pact with the devil Mephisto, who first appears as a poodle (“so that was the poodle’s core!”).
78698.m: Goethe’s “Faust” is the best-known drama in German literature.

78699.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78699.e: In Friedrich Dürrenmatt’s play (1956) an old billionairess arrives by train in her impoverished home village of Güllen and offers money on a terrible condition.
78699.m: Dürrenmatt’s “The Visit” shows how money corrupts the morals of a community.

78700.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78700.e: In Dürrenmatt’s comedy (1962) three physicists live in a mental asylum; one of them wants to hide dangerous formulas from the world.
78700.m: Dürrenmatt’s “The Physicists” is about the responsibility of science.

78701.q: Which play do these emojis show?
78701.e: In Max Frisch’s play (1958) Mr Biedermann takes two strangers into his house, even though they store drums of petrol in his attic.
78701.m: Max Frisch’s “The Fire Raisers” warns against blindly looking away.

78702.q: Which play do these emojis stand for?
78702.e: In Samuel Beckett’s play two men wait in vain by a bare tree for someone who never comes.
78702.m: In “Waiting for Godot” they wait for someone who never turns up.

78703.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78703.e: Claude Nobs founded the jazz festival on the shore of Lake Geneva in Montreux in 1967.
78703.m: The Montreux Jazz Festival has taken place on Lake Geneva since 1967.

78704.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78704.e: The Gurtenfestival takes place on the Gurten, Bern’s local mountain; the bear stands for Bern.
78704.m: The Gurtenfestival takes place on Bern’s local mountain.

78705.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78705.e: Since 1992, Love Mobiles with techno music have been driving around the lake basin in Zurich at the Street Parade; often around 900,000 visitors come.
78705.m: The Street Parade is a huge techno party on Lake Zurich.

78706.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78706.e: The Berlinale takes place every February; the main prize is the Golden Bear.
78706.m: At the Berlinale the best film wins the Golden Bear.

78707.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78707.e: At the film festival on the Côte d’Azur the main prize awarded is the Palme d’Or (Golden Palm).
78707.m: In Cannes the best film wins the Palme d’Or.

78708.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78708.e: The Venice Film Festival (since 1932) is the oldest in the world; the main prize is the Golden Lion, and the gondola stands for Venice.
78708.m: In Venice the best film wins the Golden Lion.

78709.q: Which festival do these emojis stand for?
78709.e: The Lucerne Festival brings classical orchestras to Lucerne, the city of the Lion Monument on Lake Lucerne.
78709.m: The Lucerne Festival is one of the most important festivals of classical music.

78710.q: Which festival do these emojis show?
78710.e: At the Salzburg Festival, Hofmannsthal’s “Jedermann” (Everyman), a play about a rich man and death, has been performed in front of the cathedral since 1920.
78710.m: “Jedermann” has been performed in front of Salzburg Cathedral every summer since 1920.

78711.q: Which Swiss painter do these emojis stand for?
78711.e: Around 1910 Ferdinand Hodler painted “The Woodcutter”; from 1911 the image appeared on the Swiss 50-franc note.
78711.m: Hodler’s “Woodcutter” could be seen on the 50-franc note for decades.

78712.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78712.e: Alberto Giacometti created long, thin figures such as “Walking Man”; he appeared on the 100-franc note of the 8th series.
78712.m: Giacometti is famous for his thin, elongated bronze figures.

78713.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78713.e: Jean Tinguely built moving machine sculptures from cogwheels and scrap; in Basel his figures spray water in the Tinguely Fountain.
78713.m: Tinguely built machines that move and make noise.

78714.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78714.e: In 1936 Meret Oppenheim covered a cup, saucer and spoon with gazelle fur; the object “Breakfast in Fur” made her world-famous.
78714.m: Meret Oppenheim became world-famous with her fur-covered cup.

78715.q: Which artist do these emojis stand for?
78715.e: The clover leaf stands for the name Klee (German for clover); in 1925 Paul Klee painted the picture “The Goldfish”. The Zentrum Paul Klee is in Bern.
78715.m: Paul Klee grew up in Bern, where the Zentrum Paul Klee stands today.

78716.q: Which Swiss artist do these emojis stand for?
78716.e: Sophie Taeuber-Arp from Davos danced with the Dadaists, taught textile design and created pictures of triangles, circles and rectangles; she was on the 50-franc note of the 8th series.
78716.m: Sophie Taeuber-Arp was a dancer, textile artist and painter of geometric pictures.

78717.q: Which painter do these emojis stand for?
78717.e: Giovanni Segantini painted the Engadine in the bright mountain sunlight; his Alpine triptych “Life, Nature, Death” hangs in the Segantini Museum in St Moritz.
78717.m: Segantini’s Alpine triptych can be seen in the Segantini Museum in St Moritz.

78718.q: Which song do these emojis stand for?
78718.e: In 1841 Alberich Zwyssig set to music the text by Leonhard Widmer, which begins with the red dawn; since 1981 the Swiss Psalm has officially been the national anthem of Switzerland.
78718.m: The Swiss Psalm has been Switzerland’s official national anthem since 1981.

78719.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78719.e: Basel Carnival begins at 4 am with the Morgestraich: the lights go out, and groups called cliques march through the city with drums and lanterns.
78719.m: The Morgestraich at 4 am opens Basel Carnival.

78720.q: Which Swiss festival do these emojis show?
78720.e: The winegrowers’ festival in Vevey takes place only about every 20 to 25 years, most recently in 2019 in an arena with 20,000 seats; since 2016 it has been UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.
78720.m: The Fête des Vignerons in Vevey is celebrated only about once a generation.

78721.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78721.e: In Liestal, on the Sunday of carnival, burning bundles of wood (Chienbäse) and fire wagons are carried and pulled through the old town at night.
78721.m: At Chienbäse, burning wagons are pulled through the town gate in Liestal.

78722.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78722.e: In January in Basel, the Wild Man travels down the Rhine on a raft with a small fir tree; with the griffin (Vogel Gryff) and the lion he dances through Kleinbasel.
78722.m: At Vogel Gryff the griffin, the lion and the Wild Man dance through Kleinbasel.

78723.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis stand for?
78723.e: In Hornussen the puck (Nouss) is hit far across a field and buzzes like a hornet; the opponents stop it with wooden boards.
78723.m: In Hornussen the team stops the Nouss with wooden boards.

78724.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis show?
78724.e: In stone throwing, the Unspunnen stone, which weighs about 83.5 kilograms, is thrown as far as possible.
78724.m: The Unspunnen stone weighs about 83.5 kilograms.

78725.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78725.e: At the Eierläset after Easter, runners collect raw eggs from little piles of sawdust and throw them to a catcher with a big basket; the faster team wins.
78725.m: At the Eierläset, spring beats winter in a race with raw eggs.

78726.q: Which Swiss tradition do these emojis show?
78726.e: In the Justistal near Sigriswil, the summer’s alpine cheese is shared out in September: each farmer gets as much cheese as his cows gave milk.
78726.m: At the Chästeilet, the alpine cheese is shared out according to how much milk the cows gave.

78727.q: Which Swiss custom do these emojis stand for?
78727.e: In Appenzell Ausserrhoden, on 31 December and 13 January, the “beautiful”, the “ugly” and the “beautiful-ugly” Chläuse go from farm to farm with bells and large headdresses.
78727.m: The Silvesterchläuse walk through the Appenzell region with bells and headdresses.

78728.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78728.e: Price tags and two falling curves show that prices in the shops are generally going down. A lasting fall in the price level is called deflation.
78728.m: In deflation, the general price level falls over a longer period.

78729.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78729.e: The factory with a falling curve and the worker with a cross stand for shrinking production and job cuts. When economic output shrinks over several quarters, it is called a recession.
78729.m: In a recession, economic output shrinks and jobs are lost.

78730.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78730.e: The goods (parcel) and the customers (raised hand) are on the two sides of a pair of scales. How supply and demand balance out determines the price in a free market.
78730.m: In a free market, supply and demand determine the price.

78731.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78731.e: Three workers each do a different task: screwing, painting, packing. Splitting work into separate steps like this is called division of labour; Adam Smith described it in 1776 using the example of pin making.
78731.m: With division of labour, each person specialises in one step.

78732.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78732.e: A coin, shopping bags and a muscle stand for money, buying and power. Purchasing power tells you how many goods you can buy with a certain amount of money.
78732.m: Purchasing power shows how much you can afford with your money.

78733.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78733.e: The factory and the curves that rise and fall in turn, with the circular arrow, show a recurring up and down. This regular rise and fall of the economy is called the business cycle.
78733.m: The business cycle describes the recurring ups and downs of the economy.

78734.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78734.e: Money flows from the state (government building) to a farm (tractor). Financial support like this from the state, without anything given directly in return, is called a subsidy.
78734.m: A subsidy is state money to help particular businesses or industries.

78735.q: Which economic term do these pictures stand for?
78735.e: An idea (light bulb), a rocket and an office building stand for a new company that wants to grow fast with an innovative idea. Young companies like this are called start-ups.
78735.m: A start-up is a young company with a new business idea.

78736.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78736.e: Parliament passes a law, the people raise their hands, collect signatures and vote. In Switzerland an optional referendum needs 50,000 signatures within 100 days.
78736.m: With a referendum, the people can vote on a law passed by parliament.

78737.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78737.e: A signed letter is sent by post to an authority. In Switzerland anyone may send a request or suggestion to the authorities with a petition (Art. 33 of the Federal Constitution).
78737.m: A petition is a written request to an authority that anyone may submit.

78738.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78738.e: A red party and a blue party shake hands in parliament. Such an alliance of several parties, usually to govern together, is called a coalition.
78738.m: A coalition is an alliance of parties that govern together.

78739.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78739.e: The ballot box, the finger on the lips and the lock show that nobody may find out how someone votes. The secret ballot protects free voting.
78739.m: The secret ballot guarantees that nobody finds out how you voted.

78740.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78740.e: A megaphone and a newspaper spread lies that are meant to get into people’s heads. Propaganda is the deliberate, often one-sided or false influencing of many people’s opinions.
78740.m: Propaganda tries to influence people’s opinions deliberately and one-sidedly.

78741.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78741.e: Something is cut out of a newspaper and banned. When the state suppresses content before or after publication, it is called censorship; the Federal Constitution forbids it (Art. 17).
78741.m: Censorship means that content is suppressed or banned.

78742.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78742.e: The ballot box and the boxing glove together stand for an election and a fight. In an election campaign, parties and candidates compete for votes before an election.
78742.m: In an election campaign, parties compete for people’s votes before an election.

78743.q: Which political term do these pictures stand for?
78743.e: A newspaper, an open lock, a fountain pen and a microphone stand for media that may report freely. Freedom of the press (in Switzerland called media freedom) is a fundamental right.
78743.m: Thanks to freedom of the press, the media may report independently.

78744.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78744.e: Whoever writes (hand with pen) creates a work like a book; the copyright symbol and the scales stand for legal protection. In Switzerland copyright usually protects works until 70 years after the author’s death.
78744.m: Copyright protects creative works such as books, music and pictures.

78745.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
78745.e: In court (scales) a person counts as innocent (angel face) as long as their guilt has not been proven (question mark, magnifying glass). This principle is called the presumption of innocence and is in Art. 32 of the Federal Constitution.
78745.m: Because of the presumption of innocence, everyone counts as innocent until proven guilty.

78746.q: Which legal term do these pictures stand for?
