79447.q: What do you knead salt dough for crafts from?
79447.e: Salt dough is kneaded from flour, salt and water. After drying or baking it goes hard, and you can paint it.
79447.m: Salt dough is made from flour, salt and water.

79448.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
79448.e: In Switzerland, sugar beet grows in many fields. Sugar is made from its juice.
79448.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

79449.q: In which place in the canton of Bern is there a large Swiss sugar factory?
79449.e: Sugar has been made in Aarberg for over 100 years. A second sugar factory is in Frauenfeld.
79449.m: There is a sugar factory in Aarberg.

79450.q: What happens if you stir a lot of sugar into a small glass of water?
79450.e: Water can only dissolve a certain amount of sugar. Anything extra stays at the bottom as grains.
79450.m: Water cannot dissolve endless amounts of sugar.

79451.q: Which plant is much sugar made from in warm countries?
79451.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass that grows in warm countries. Its stalks are full of sweet juice.
79451.m: In warm countries, sugar is made from sugar cane.

79452.q: Which sugar is as fine as flour?
79452.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It is used for dusting or for icing.
79452.m: Icing sugar is as fine as flour.

79453.q: What can lots of sweets cause in your teeth?
79453.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can attack the teeth and cause tooth decay.
79453.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

79454.q: What is sugar pressed into little blocks called?
79454.e: Sugar cubes are made of pressed sugar crystals. This makes them easy to count.

79455.e: Green leaves make sugar with sunlight, water and air. The plant stores it, for example, in fruits or roots.
79455.m: Plants make sugar in their green leaves.

79456.q: What do you get when a machine spins melted sugar into fine threads?
79456.e: The machine melts sugar and spins it through tiny holes. The threads set at once and form a cloud.
79456.m: Candyfloss is made of fine sugar threads.

79457.q: What do you sprinkle on crème brûlée before browning it with a flame?
79457.e: Under the hot flame, the sugar melts and turns brown. This makes a crunchy crust on top.
79457.m: Sugar is sprinkled on crème brûlée.

79458.q: What is melted brown sugar called?
79458.e: When sugar is heated strongly, it melts and turns brown. This is called caramel.
79458.m: Brown, melted sugar is called caramel.

79459.q: What does sugar smell like when it caramelises?
79459.e: When sugar caramelises, new scents are formed. That is why it smells sweet and slightly toasted.

79460.q: What happens if you heat caramel for far too long?
79460.e: Sugar heated for too long burns. Then it turns black and tastes bitter.
79460.m: Caramel that gets too hot burns and turns bitter.

79461.q: Why is liquid caramel in the pan dangerous?
a: It is hotter than boiling water
79461.e: Caramel only forms well above 100 degrees. It sticks to the skin and burns it badly.

79462.q: Which Swiss dessert has a caramel sauce?
79462.e: Caramelköpfli is a pudding with a brown caramel sauce. You turn it out onto a plate.

79463.q: What happens to liquid caramel when it cools down?
79463.e: As it cools, liquid caramel sets and becomes as hard as glass. This is how hard sweets are made.

79464.q: Which fairground treat has a coating of caramel?
79464.e: Caramelised almonds are heated with sugar in a pan. The sugar caramelises and coats the almonds.
79464.m: Caramelised almonds have a caramel coating.

79465.q: Which Swiss sweet is made by boiling sugar and cream until it is light brown?
79465.e: For Rahmtäfeli, sugar is boiled with cream and butter. The sugar caramelises and turns the mixture brown.
79465.m: Rahmtäfeli are made from sugar and cream.

79466.q: Why does a cut apple with lemon juice turn brown more slowly?
a: The juice slows down the browning
79466.e: In the air, the flesh of the fruit turns brown. Lemon juice slows this change down.
79466.m: Lemon juice keeps apples pale for longer.

79467.q: Which vitamin is lemon juice especially rich in?
79467.e: Lemons are rich in vitamin C. The body needs it, for example, to fight off illness.
79467.m: Lemons contain a lot of vitamin C.

79468.q: What happens when you pour lemon juice into milk?
79468.e: The acid in the lemon makes the protein in the milk clump together. White flakes form.

79469.q: What happens to a dark, tarnished copper coin when you rub it with lemon juice and salt?
79469.e: The acid in lemon juice dissolves the dark layer on the coin. The shiny metal underneath appears again.
79469.m: Lemon juice makes dark copper shiny again.

79470.q: Where in a lemon is the strong-smelling oil?
79470.e: The lemon peel contains tiny oil glands. If you grate the peel, it smells strongly of lemon.
79470.m: The scented oil is in the lemon peel.

79471.q: What can you produce with a lemon, a piece of copper and a piece of zinc?
79471.e: The sour juice and the two metals together form a simple battery. It supplies a tiny bit of electricity.
79471.m: You can build a battery with a lemon.

79472.q: Which group of fruits does the lemon belong to?
79472.e: The lemon belongs to the citrus fruits. Oranges and mandarins are citrus fruits too.
79472.m: The lemon is a citrus fruit.

79473.q: What happens when you drip lemon juice onto a piece of limestone?
a: The stone goes soft like wax
79473.e: The acid in lemon juice attacks the limestone. This produces a gas that forms little bubbles.

79474.q: What happens when you pour sherbet powder into water?
79474.e: In water, the substances in the sherbet powder react with each other. This forms lots of gas bubbles.

79475.q: Which two substances in sherbet powder fizz together?
a: Bicarbonate of soda and an acid
79475.e: Sherbet powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid. Together with water they make gas.
79475.m: Bicarbonate of soda and acid make sherbet powder fizz.

79476.q: Which acid is often found in sherbet powder?
79476.e: Sherbet powder usually contains citric acid or tartaric acid. It also gives the slightly sour taste.
79476.m: Sherbet powder often contains citric acid.

79477.q: What do you feel when you sprinkle sherbet powder on your tongue?
79477.e: Saliva is moist. That is why the sherbet powder starts to fizz and tingle on your tongue.
79477.m: Sherbet powder tingles on the tongue.

79478.q: Why must sherbet powder be kept dry?
a: Otherwise it fizzes in the tin
79478.e: Moisture starts the reaction. Then the powder is used up before you put it in the glass.

79479.q: What is a pressed tablet that fizzes in water called?
79479.e: An effervescent tablet contains the same substances as sherbet powder. It is just pressed tightly together.

79480.e: Besides bicarbonate of soda and acid, sherbet powder contains sugar. It gives the sweet taste.

79481.q: Where does sherbet powder fizz faster, in warm or in cold water?
79481.e: In warm water, chemical reactions happen faster. That is why sherbet powder fizzes more strongly there and is finished sooner.
79481.m: Sherbet powder fizzes faster in warm water.

79482.e: Lactic acid bacteria eat the milk sugar. As they do, they make acid, and the milk goes sour.

79483.q: Which acid forms in soured milk?
79483.e: The bacteria turn the milk sugar into lactic acid. This acid gets its name from milk (Latin ‘lac’).
79483.m: Lactic acid forms in soured milk.

79484.q: How does milk change when it goes sour?
79484.e: The acid makes the protein in the milk curdle. That is why soured milk gets thicker.

79485.q: Which dairy product is made with the help of lactic acid bacteria?
79485.e: To make yoghurt, lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They make the milk sour and thick.
79485.m: Yoghurt is made with lactic acid bacteria.

79486.q: Where does milk go sour fastest?
79486.e: Bacteria multiply quickly in the warmth. In the fridge they work only slowly.
79486.m: Milk goes sour quickly in the warmth.

79487.q: What does soured milk taste like?
79487.e: Soured milk contains lactic acid. That is why it tastes slightly sour.

79488.q: What do you get when you let soured, thick milk drain?
79488.e: As it drains, the liquid runs away. A thick, white mass is left behind: quark.
79488.m: Quark is made from soured milk.

79489.q: What is the yellowish liquid that separates from soured milk called?
79489.e: When milk curdles, a yellowish liquid separates off. This liquid is called whey.
79489.m: The liquid from curdled milk is called whey.

79490.q: What happens to egg white when it is cooked?
79490.e: Raw egg white is see-through and runny. The heat makes it white and firm.
79490.m: Cooked egg white turns white and firm.

79491.q: About how long do you boil a hard-boiled egg?
79491.e: A medium egg is hard after about 10 minutes in boiling water. A soft-boiled egg needs only about 5 minutes.
79491.m: A hard-boiled egg boils for about 10 minutes.

79492.q: Can you make a boiled egg raw again?
79492.e: When cooked, the egg white changes for ever. This change cannot be undone.
79492.m: A boiled egg never becomes raw again.

79493.q: How does a hard-boiled egg spin on the table?
79493.e: Everything inside a hard-boiled egg is solid, so it spins like a top. A raw egg wobbles because the inside sloshes about.
79493.m: A hard-boiled egg spins like a top.

79494.q: Why do you put eggs in cold water after boiling them?
a: So they take in more salt
79494.e: A hot egg keeps cooking even outside the pan. Cold water cools it down quickly.

79495.q: What does the yolk get if you boil an egg for far too long?
79495.e: If boiled too long, substances from the white and the yolk react with each other. This produces a greenish rim.
79495.m: Eggs boiled too long have a green rim.

79496.q: Why are eggs often pricked before boiling?
79496.e: There is a small air bubble inside an egg. Through the hole, the air can escape when heated, and the shell cracks less often.

79497.q: Which sets first when cooking, the egg white or the yolk?
79497.e: The egg white is on the outside and gets hot first. It also sets at a slightly lower temperature than the yolk.
79497.m: When cooking, the egg white sets first.

79498.q: Which cereal is popcorn made from?
79498.e: Popcorn is made from a special kind of maize. The kernels burst open when heated.

79499.q: What is inside a maize kernel that turns to steam when heated?
79499.e: Inside the kernel there is some water. When heated, it turns into hot steam.
79499.m: A maize kernel contains a little water.

79500.q: Why does a maize kernel burst open when heated?
a: The kernel is cut from the outside
The oil presses from the outside
79500.e: The steam inside the kernel presses harder and harder against the hard shell. At some point it suddenly splits open.
79500.m: Steam bursts the maize kernel open.

79501.q: What is the kind of maize used to make popcorn called?
79501.e: Popping corn has an especially hard shell. That is why enough pressure can build up inside.
79501.m: Popcorn is made from popping corn.

79502.q: Why does a maize kernel with a crack in its shell not pop properly?
79502.e: The steam can slowly escape through the crack. So no pressure builds up to burst the kernel.
79502.m: A kernel with a crack does not pop properly.

79503.q: What do you hear when popcorn pops in the pan?
79503.e: Each kernel bursts open with a small bang. That is why the pan keeps popping.
79503.m: Popcorn pops as it bursts open.

79504.q: How does a maize kernel change when it becomes popcorn?
79504.e: When it bursts, the soft inside of the kernel puffs up. The popcorn is much bigger than the kernel was before.
79504.m: Popcorn is much bigger than the maize kernel.

79505.q: Where does maize originally come from?
79505.e: Maize was first grown in Central America. Only later did it come to Europe.

79506.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when making popcorn?
a: So the kernels don't jump out
79506.e: The bursting kernels jump up. With the lid they stay in the pan, and hot oil does not spatter out.
79506.m: A lid keeps the popcorn in the pan.

79507.q: Which parts of the sunflower is sunflower oil pressed from?
79507.e: Sunflower seeds contain a lot of oil. It is pressed out in an oil mill.
79507.m: Sunflower oil comes from the seeds.

79508.q: Which yellow-flowering field crop is most home-grown cooking oil in Switzerland pressed from?
79508.e: In spring, many rapeseed fields bloom yellow in Switzerland. Rapeseed oil is pressed from the small seeds.
79508.m: A lot of rapeseed oil is made in Switzerland.

79509.q: Which oil is made from the fruit of trees around the Mediterranean?
79509.e: Olive trees grow mainly around the Mediterranean. Olive oil is pressed from their fruit.

79510.q: What does a drop of oil leave on paper?
79510.e: Oil soaks into the paper and does not evaporate like water. That is why a see-through grease spot is left.
79510.m: Oil leaves a grease spot on paper.

79511.q: Why is cooking oil best kept in a dark, cool place?
79511.e: Light, warmth and air change the oil over time. Then it smells and tastes rancid.
79511.m: Keep cooking oil dark and cool.

79512.q: What does oil feel like between your fingers?
79512.e: Oil makes the skin smooth and slippery. That is why it feels slippery.

79513.q: Where should old cooking oil go?
79513.e: Oil blocks pipes and pollutes water. That is why you take it to a collection point in a bottle.
79513.m: Old oil goes to a collection point.

79514.q: What often happens to olive oil in the fridge?
79514.e: In the cold, some fats in olive oil go solid. That is why it goes cloudy and thick, but clear again when warm.
79514.m: Olive oil goes cloudy in the cold.

79515.e: Chips are deep-fried in hot oil. The oil is much hotter than boiling water and makes them crispy.
79515.m: Chips are fried in hot oil.

79516.q: Which part of a door is a lever?
79516.e: The door handle turns around a pivot. When you press down on its end, it pulls the latch back into the lock with little force.
79516.m: The door handle is a lever.

79517.q: What is the point a lever turns around called?
79517.e: Every lever has a pivot. The bar moves around this point.
79517.m: A lever turns around its pivot.

79518.q: Where do you push on a lever to need the least force?
79518.e: The longer the distance from the pivot to your hand, the less force you need. That is why you hold a lever far out.
79518.m: Far from the pivot you need little force.

79519.q: Which famous Greek is said to have claimed he could move the world with a lever?
79519.e: Archimedes studied the lever more than 2,000 years ago. He is said to have claimed that, given a fixed point, he could move the world.

79520.q: Which kitchen tool is a lever for opening bottles?
79520.e: The bottle opener rests against the cap and levers it up. So you only need a little force.
79520.m: A bottle opener is a lever.

79521.q: Which part of your body works like a lever when you lift a bag?
79521.e: The forearm turns around the elbow joint as if around a pivot. The muscles pull on it like on a lever.
79521.m: Your arm works like a lever.

79522.q: What do you use a crowbar for?
79522.e: A crowbar is a long steel lever. You can use it to prise open crates or loosen stuck boards.
79522.m: A crowbar is a long lever.

79523.q: Which part of a bike is a lever?
79523.e: The brake lever turns around a pivot. With little finger strength it pulls hard on the brake cable.
79523.m: The brake lever on a bike is a lever.

79524.q: What is the distance from the pivot to the point where the force acts called?
79524.e: This distance is called the lever arm. A long lever arm makes the work easier.
79524.m: A long lever arm saves force.

79525.q: What does a screw have that a nail does not?
79525.e: A groove winds around the screw: the thread. A nail, on the other hand, is smooth.

79526.q: Why does a screw hold well in wood?
79526.e: As you turn it in, the thread cuts into the wood. That is why the screw cannot simply be pulled out.
79526.m: The thread holds the screw in place.

79527.q: What is the part with a thread on the inside that you turn onto a bolt called?
79527.e: A nut has a thread on the inside. You turn it onto the bolt and use it to hold parts tightly together.
79527.m: You turn a nut onto a bolt.

79528.q: Which way do you turn a normal screw to screw it in?
79528.e: Most screws have a right-hand thread. You turn them clockwise to screw them in and anticlockwise to take them out.

79529.q: What do you put into a hole drilled in a concrete wall so the screw holds?
79529.e: The wall plug spreads out as the screw is turned in. So it holds firmly in the hard concrete.
79529.m: A wall plug holds the screw in the wall.

79530.q: Which simple machine is wrapped around a screw?
79530.e: The thread is like a sloping ramp winding around the shank. So a screw is a rolled-up inclined plane.
79530.m: A thread is a rolled-up inclined plane.

79531.q: What does the head of a screw often have so the tool can grip it?
79531.e: The tip of the tool fits into the slot or the cross. That way you can turn the screw.
79531.m: The screw head has a slot or a cross.

79532.q: Which device turns screws in with a motor?
79532.e: A cordless screwdriver has a motor and a battery. It drives screws in quickly and without much effort.
79532.m: A cordless screwdriver turns screws with a motor.

79533.q: What does the front end of a wood screw look like?
79533.e: A wood screw is pointed at the front. That way it easily finds its way into the wood.
79533.m: A wood screw is pointed at the front.

79535.q: What is a block and tackle made of?
79535.e: A rope runs over several pulleys. The load hangs from the pulleys and is pulled up.
79535.m: A block and tackle has pulleys and a rope.

79536.q: What do you save with a block and tackle?
79536.e: With several pulleys, the load is shared between several sections of rope. That is why you need less force to pull.
79536.m: A block and tackle saves force.

79537.q: What is the trade-off for the force you save with a block and tackle?
a: You have to pull more rope
79537.e: What you save in force, you have to make up for by pulling further. With half the force you pull twice as much rope.
79537.m: Less force means pulling more rope.

79538.q: What does a single fixed pulley on the ceiling do?
a: It changes the direction of pull
79538.e: With a fixed pulley you pull down and the load goes up. But it does not save any force.
79538.m: A fixed pulley only changes the direction of pull.

79539.q: Where do you often find a block and tackle?
79539.e: Building cranes lift heavy loads with ropes and pulleys. That is why they have a block and tackle.
79539.m: Building cranes have a block and tackle.

79540.q: A load hangs from two supporting sections of rope. Roughly how much force do you need?
79540.e: The two sections of rope carry the load together. So you only need to use about half the force.
79540.m: Two sections of rope halve the force.

79541.q: What is a pulley that moves up with the load called?
79541.e: A movable pulley hangs on the load and moves with it. A fixed pulley, on the other hand, stays in its place.
79541.m: A movable pulley moves up with the load.

79542.q: What does a wedge do when you hammer it into a piece of wood?
79542.e: The wedge pushes the wood apart to the sides. So the piece of wood splits.

a: Thin at the front, thick at the back
79543.e: A wedge is thin or pointed at the front and gets thicker towards the back. That way it pushes things apart.
79543.m: A wedge is thin at the front and thick at the back.

79544.q: What holds the head of a hammer firmly on the handle?
79544.e: At the top of the handle there is a small wedge made of wood or metal. It pushes the wood apart, so the head sits tightly.
79544.m: A wedge holds the hammer head on the handle.

79545.q: Which part of a knife works like a wedge?
79545.e: When you cut, the blade pushes the food apart like a wedge. The handle is only for holding.
79545.m: A knife blade is a wedge.

79546.q: Why do you jam a wedge under a door?
79546.e: The doorstop wedge jams between the floor and the door. So the door cannot swing shut.
79546.m: A door wedge keeps the door open.

79547.q: Which teeth work like wedges when you bite something off?
79547.e: The incisors at the front are thin and sharp. They push into an apple like wedges.

79548.q: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
79548.e: A sharp edge is a very thin wedge. It goes in with little force.
79548.m: A thin wedge goes in more easily.

79549.q: What do you put behind the wheels of a parked trailer so it does not roll away?
79549.e: The wheel chock jams between the wheel and the ground. So the trailer cannot start rolling.
79549.m: A wheel chock holds wheels in place.

79550.q: Which end of a nail works like a wedge?
79550.e: The point of the nail is thin and gets thicker towards the back. It pushes the wood fibres apart like a wedge.
79550.m: The point of a nail works like a wedge.

79551.q: What rolls down an inclined plane by itself?
79551.e: A round ball rolls down a sloping surface by itself. Things with edges, like a dice or a book, often just stay put.
79551.m: A ball rolls down an inclined plane.

79552.q: Why is it better to roll a heavy barrel up a ramp onto a lorry?
79552.e: On the ramp you do not have to lift the barrel straight up. You push it up bit by bit and need less force.

79553.q: What is the disadvantage of a very gentle ramp?
79553.e: The gentler the ramp, the less force you need. But the way up is longer.
79553.m: A gentle ramp means a long way.

79554.q: Why do many mountain pass roads in the Alps climb in lots of bends?
79554.e: A straight road up the mountain would be far too steep. With lots of hairpin bends the road gets longer, but less steep.
79554.m: Bends make mountain roads less steep.

79555.q: Who are ramps next to stairs built for?
79555.e: On wheels you cannot get up stairs. On a ramp, wheelchairs and pushchairs can roll up.

79556.q: Where does a ball roll down faster?
79556.e: The steeper the ramp, the more strongly the ball is pulled down. That is why it rolls faster on the steep ramp.
79556.m: Things roll faster on steep ramps.

79557.q: Which piece of playground equipment is an inclined plane?
79557.e: The slide is a sloping surface. You slide down it from the top to the bottom.
79557.m: A slide is an inclined plane.

79558.q: What pulls a sledge down a snowy slope?
79558.e: The Earth pulls everything downwards. On the sloping hill, this gravity gets the sledge sliding.
79558.m: Gravity pulls the sledge down the slope.

79559.q: What do you call several gears that mesh together and pass on a turning movement?
79559.e: Several gears that mesh together form a gear train. It passes the turning movement from one wheel to the next.
79559.m: Meshing gears form a gear train.

79560.q: A gear turns to the right. Which way does the gear meshing directly with it turn?
79560.e: When two gears mesh, they turn in opposite directions. If one turns right, the other turns left.
79560.m: Two gears turn in opposite directions.

79561.q: A small gear meshes with a big one. Which one turns faster?
79561.e: The small gear has fewer teeth. It has to turn more often before the big one has gone round once.

79562.q: Where do you find lots of tiny gears?
79562.e: In mechanical watches, lots of small gears turn the hands. Switzerland is famous for such watches.
79562.m: Mechanical watches contain lots of gears.

79563.q: What connects the front and rear sprockets on a bike?
79563.e: The bike chain runs over both sprockets. That way pedalling drives the back wheel.
79563.m: The chain connects the sprockets on a bike.

79564.q: What are the gears on a bike for?
a: So you can pedal uphill more easily
79564.e: The gears switch between sprockets. In an easy gear you pedal uphill with less force.
79564.m: With gears you ride uphill more easily.

79565.q: Which kitchen tool with a crank has a small gear that turns the tin along its rim?
79565.e: When you turn the crank, a small gear grips the rim of the tin. It turns the tin while a little wheel cuts the lid open.
79565.m: A tin opener with a crank has a gear.

79566.q: Why do the teeth of two meshing gears have to be the same size?
a: So they fit into each other
79566.e: Only teeth of the same size fit neatly into the gaps of the other wheel. Otherwise the gears jam or slip.
79566.m: Meshing gears need teeth of the same size.

79567.q: Three gears mesh in a row. How does the third turn compared with the first?
79567.e: The second wheel turns against the first, and the third turns against the second again. So the first and third turn the same way.
79567.m: The first and third gears turn the same way.

79568.q: What do you mainly use a hammer for?
79568.e: With the heavy head of the hammer you knock nails into wood. The swing gives a lot of force.
79568.m: You knock in nails with a hammer.

79569.q: Which hammer has a soft head so nothing gets scratched?
79569.e: The rubber mallet strikes softly. That way you can knock parts together without damaging them.

79570.q: What is the split side of a claw hammer for?
79570.e: The claw grips under the head of the nail. You pull the nail out as if with a lever.
79570.m: You pull nails out with the claw.

79571.q: What is a very heavy hammer that you swing with both hands called?
79571.e: The sledgehammer has a big, heavy head and a long handle. You use it, for example, to drive posts into the ground.

79572.q: Where do you hold the hammer handle to strike hard?
a: At the end of the handle
In the middle of the head
79572.e: If you hold the handle at the end, the head swings in a big arc. So it strikes with more momentum.
79572.m: For hard blows, hold the hammer at the end.

79573.q: What protects your eyes from splinters when hammering?
79573.e: When hammering, small splinters can fly off. Safety goggles protect your eyes.

79574.q: Which craftsperson hammers glowing iron on an anvil?
79574.e: The blacksmith makes iron glowing hot and soft in the fire. Then he shapes it with a hammer on the anvil.
79574.m: The blacksmith shapes iron with a hammer.

79575.q: What is the part of a hammer you hold in your hand called?
79575.e: You hold a hammer by its handle. The handle is often made of wood or plastic.
79575.m: You hold a hammer by its handle.

79576.q: What do you use a screwdriver for?
79576.e: The tip of the screwdriver fits into the screw head. When you turn the handle, the screw turns.
79576.m: You turn screws with a screwdriver.

79578.q: Which screwdriver fits a screw with a cross in its head?
79578.e: For a cross in the screw head you need a cross-shaped tip. A flat-head screwdriver would slip.
79578.m: Cross-head screws need a cross-head screwdriver.

79579.q: Why does a screwdriver have a thick handle?
a: So you have more force when turning
79579.e: A thick handle works like a big wheel. With it you can turn the thin tip with more force.
79579.m: A thick handle gives more force when turning.

79580.q: What often happens if the screwdriver does not fit the screw exactly?
79580.e: A tip that does not fit does not sit firmly in the screw head. It slips and can damage the head.
79580.m: A screwdriver that does not fit slips.

79581.q: Which tool is built into many Swiss army knives?
79581.e: Besides the blade, many Swiss army knives have small tools. These often include a small screwdriver.
79581.m: Many pocket knives have a small screwdriver.

79582.q: What are the small, interchangeable tips for a screwdriver called?
79582.e: Bits are short tips that you put into a holder. That way one handle fits many screws.
79582.m: Interchangeable screwdriver tips are called bits.

79583.q: Why do electricians’ screwdrivers have a plastic coating on the shaft?
79583.e: Plastic does not conduct electricity. So your hand is protected when you work on electrical parts.

79584.q: What does a saw have on its blade?
79584.e: The saw blade has lots of sharp teeth. As it moves back and forth, they tear small pieces out of the wood.

79585.q: What is produced when you saw wood?
79585.e: The teeth of the saw tear out tiny pieces of wood. These fall to the floor as sawdust.

79586.q: What is a saw with a motor and a moving chain called?
79586.e: On a chainsaw, a chain with teeth runs round very fast. Foresters use it to fell trees.

79587.q: Which fine saw do you use in craft lessons to cut curves in thin wood?
79587.e: The fretsaw has a very thin blade. You can use it to cut even tight curves.
79587.m: You cut curves with a fretsaw.

79589.q: Which saw do you use to cut through a metal pipe?
79589.e: A hacksaw has a hard blade with very fine teeth. That way it can cut even metal.
79589.m: You saw metal with a hacksaw.

79590.q: What do you use to clamp a board to the table before sawing?
79590.e: The G-clamp presses the board firmly against the table. So it does not slip while you saw.
79590.m: A G-clamp holds the board in place.

79591.q: What do you use pliers for?
79591.e: With pliers you can grip small things firmly, bend them or snip them off. Your fingers alone would not have enough strength.

79592.q: Which tool do you use to pull nails out?
79592.e: Pincers have two sharp jaws. You grip the nail head with them and lever it out.
79592.m: You pull nails out with pincers.

79593.q: Why are the handles of pliers much longer than their jaws?
79593.e: Pliers are made of two levers. Long handles turn a little hand strength into a big force at the front.
79593.m: Long handles give pliers a lot of force.

79594.q: Which pliers have long, thin jaws for small parts?
79594.e: Needle-nose pliers have narrow, long jaws. With them you can reach even tight spots.

79595.q: Which tool do you use to cut through thin wires?
79595.e: Side cutters have two sharp cutting edges. You can easily snip wires with them.

79596.q: Which tool do you use to turn sausages on the barbecue?
79596.e: Barbecue tongs are long. So your hands stay far away from the heat.
79596.m: You turn sausages with barbecue tongs.

79597.q: What do you pick up with sugar tongs?
79597.e: With the little sugar tongs you take sugar cubes out of the bowl. That way you do not touch them with your fingers.
79597.m: You pick up sugar cubes with sugar tongs.

79598.q: What is the place where the two halves of a pair of pliers are joined called?
79598.e: At the joint, the two halves are joined so they can turn. That is where the pivot of the two levers is.
79598.m: The two halves of pliers are joined at the joint.

79599.q: What is the container of a wheelbarrow that you shovel the load into called?
79599.e: The container of a wheelbarrow is called the tray. It is usually made of sheet metal, less often of plastic.
79599.m: The container of a wheelbarrow is called the tray.

79600.q: How do you lift a heavily loaded wheelbarrow correctly?
a: With a straight back, using your knees
79600.e: You bend your knees, keep your back straight and lift with your legs. That protects your back.
79600.m: Lift a heavy wheelbarrow with a straight back.

79601.q: Where is the pivot of the lever on a wheelbarrow?
a: In the middle of the tray
79601.e: When you lift it, the wheelbarrow turns around the axle of the wheel. So the wheel is the pivot.
79601.m: On a wheelbarrow, the wheel is the pivot.

79602.q: Where should you put the heavy load in a wheelbarrow?
a: Right at the back by the handles
79602.e: If the load is close to the wheel, the wheel carries most of it. So you need less force at the handles.
79602.m: Heavy loads belong close to the wheel.

79604.q: Why does a wheelbarrow tip over to the side easily?
79604.e: With only one wheel, the wheelbarrow does not stay upright by itself while moving. You have to keep it balanced with the handles.
79604.m: With one wheel, a wheelbarrow tips easily.

79605.q: What is the advantage of a wheelbarrow’s single wheel?
a: It is very easy to steer
79605.e: With one wheel you can turn the wheelbarrow easily. That way you get along well even on narrow paths.
79605.m: A wheelbarrow with one wheel is easy to steer.

79606.q: Who often works with a wheelbarrow?
79606.e: In the garden you often have to move soil, leaves or compost. A wheelbarrow is ideal for that.
79606.m: Gardeners often work with a wheelbarrow.

79607.q: What is a seesaw in the playground?
a: A board with a pivot in the middle
79607.e: The seesaw is a long board supported in the middle. When one child sits at each end, it goes up and down.
79607.m: A seesaw has its pivot in the middle.

79608.q: A heavy child and a light child want to seesaw. Where should the heavy child move?
79608.e: The closer you sit to the pivot, the less you push the seesaw down. That way the heavy child balances the light one.
79608.m: The heavier child sits closer to the pivot.

79609.q: Two children of the same weight sit on the seesaw. Where do they sit to be balanced?
a: The same distance from the pivot
One right at the end, one close in
79609.e: Children of the same weight need lever arms of the same length. Then the seesaw stays level.
79609.m: Children of the same weight sit equally far out.

79610.q: A heavy child and a light child both sit right at the ends. What happens?
79610.e: With lever arms of the same length, the heavier weight pushes harder. That is why the heavy child’s side sinks.
79610.m: At the same distance, the heavier side sinks.

79611.q: Which simple machine is a seesaw?
79611.e: The seesaw is a board that turns around a pivot. That is exactly how a lever works.

79612.q: What do you call it when a seesaw stays still and level?
79612.e: When both sides push equally hard, the seesaw does not move. This is called balance.
79612.m: A still, level seesaw is in balance.

79613.q: Which kind of scales works like a seesaw?
79613.e: The beam balance has a beam with a pivot in the middle. Pans hang on both sides, like two children on a seesaw.
79613.m: The beam balance works like a seesaw.

79614.q: What softens the hard bump at the bottom on many playground seesaws?
a: A rubber buffer or a tyre
79614.e: Under the seats there is often a rubber buffer or an old car tyre. So the seesaw lands softly on the ground.

79615.q: Which numbers do you write in a normal sudoku?
79615.e: In a normal sudoku you need the numbers 1, 2, 3 up to 9. Each appears exactly once in every row.
79615.m: A normal sudoku uses the numbers 1 to 9.

79616.q: How many times may a number appear in one row of a sudoku?
79616.e: In every row, each number must appear exactly once. So no number may appear twice.
79616.m: In a sudoku row, each number appears only once.

79617.q: How many squares does a normal sudoku have?
79617.e: A normal sudoku has 9 rows with 9 squares each. 9 times 9 gives 81 squares.

79618.q: How many small 3-by-3 blocks does a normal sudoku have?
79618.e: The big square is divided into 3 by 3 small blocks. That makes 9 blocks altogether.
79618.m: A sudoku is made up of 9 small blocks.

79619.q: A row of a mini sudoku with the numbers 1 to 4 contains 1, 3 and 4. Which number is missing?
79619.e: In a mini sudoku, every row needs 1, 2, 3 and 4. Only the 2 is missing.
79619.m: In a mini sudoku, the numbers 1 to 4 go in every row.

79620.q: A column of a mini sudoku with the numbers 1 to 4 contains 4, 2 and 1. Which number is missing?
79620.e: Every column needs the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. The 3 is still missing.
79620.m: In a sudoku, every column also needs all the numbers exactly once.

79621.q: A row of a normal sudoku is missing only two numbers. The row already has 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9. Which two numbers are missing?
79621.e: Of the numbers 1 to 9, the row is missing 4 and 7. The other numbers are already there.
79621.m: When you solve a sudoku, you look for the missing numbers.

79622.q: Which country does the name “sudoku” come from?
79622.e: The word sudoku is Japanese. The puzzle became famous in Japan under this name.
79622.m: The name sudoku comes from Japan.

79623.q: In a magic square, what is the same in every row, column and diagonal?
79623.e: In a magic square, all rows, columns and diagonals add up to the same number.
79623.m: In a magic square, every line has the same sum.

79624.q: In a magic square with the numbers 1 to 9, every row adds up to 15. One row is 2, 7 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79624.e: 2 + 7 = 9. To reach 15 you still need 6, because 9 + 6 = 15.
79624.m: In a magic square with 1 to 9, every line adds up to 15.

79625.q: In a magic square, every row adds up to 15. One row is 9, 5 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79625.m: You find the missing number by adding on up to the sum.

79626.q: In a magic square, every column adds up to 15. One column is 4, 3 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79626.m: In a magic square, every column also has the same sum.

79627.q: Which number is in the middle of the magic square with the numbers 1 to 9?
79627.e: 5 is the middle number of 1 to 9. In the 3-by-3 magic square it is always in the centre.
79627.m: The 5 is in the centre of the magic square with 1 to 9.

79628.q: How many squares does a magic square with 3 rows and 3 columns have?
79628.e: 3 rows with 3 squares each make 3 times 3 = 9 squares.

79629.q: In a magic square, every row adds up to 12. One row is 5, 4 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79629.m: First add up the known numbers, then add on.

79630.q: How many diagonals does a magic square have?
79630.e: One diagonal goes from top left to bottom right, the other from top right to bottom left. That makes 2 diagonals.

79631.q: In a number wall, the bottom bricks are 3 and 5. Which number goes in the brick above?
79631.e: In a number wall, you add two neighbouring bricks. 3 + 5 = 8.
79631.m: In a number wall, the top brick is the sum of the two below.

79632.q: In a number wall, the bottom bricks are 6 and 7. Which number goes in the brick above?
79632.e: You add the two bricks below: 6 + 7 = 13.
79632.m: Two neighbouring bricks added together give the brick above.

79633.q: In a number wall, the top brick is 10. The bottom left brick is 4. Which number is bottom right?
79633.e: 4 + 6 = 10. So the bottom right brick is 6.
79633.m: If a bottom brick is missing, you take the top minus the other brick.

79634.q: In a number wall, the top brick is 15. The bottom right brick is 9. Which number is bottom left?
79634.m: Subtraction helps you find a missing bottom brick.

79635.q: A number wall has the bottom bricks 1, 2 and 3. Which number is at the very top?
79635.e: The middle row is 1 + 2 = 3 and 2 + 3 = 5. At the very top is 3 + 5 = 8.
79635.m: You work out a number wall row by row from the bottom up.

79636.q: A number wall has the bottom bricks 2, 4 and 1. Which number is at the very top?
79636.e: The middle row is 2 + 4 = 6 and 4 + 1 = 5. At the very top is 6 + 5 = 11.
79636.m: In a number wall, the middle bottom brick counts twice.

79637.q: In a number wall, the bottom bricks are 20 and 30. Which number goes in the brick above?
79637.e: 20 + 30 = 50. This number goes in the brick above.
79637.m: The number wall works the same way with tens.

79638.q: A number wall has the bottom bricks 5, 5 and 5. Which number is at the very top?
79638.e: The middle row is 10 and 10. At the very top is 10 + 10 = 20.
79638.m: If the bottom bricks are the same, the middle bricks are the same too.

79639.q: In a number pyramid, you add two neighbouring numbers. At the bottom are 7 and 8. Which number goes above?
79639.e: 7 + 8 = 15. The sum goes in the box above.
79639.m: In a number pyramid, you add upwards.

79640.q: In a number pyramid, you add two neighbouring numbers. At the bottom are 4, 3 and 2. Which number is at the top?
79640.e: The middle row is 4 + 3 = 7 and 3 + 2 = 5. At the top is 7 + 5 = 12.
79640.m: The top of a number pyramid shows the result of all the steps.

79641.q: In a number pyramid, you add two neighbouring numbers. At the bottom are 10, 0 and 10. Which number is at the top?
79641.e: The middle row is 10 + 0 = 10 and 0 + 10 = 10. At the top is 10 + 10 = 20.
79641.m: Zero does not change a sum.

79642.q: In a number pyramid, the top number is 9. Below it on the left is 5. Which number is below on the right?
79642.e: 5 + 4 = 9. So the number below on the right is 4.
79642.m: Going down a number pyramid, you subtract.

79643.q: In a number pyramid, the top number is 20. Below it on the right is 12. Which number is below on the left?
79643.m: Checking with addition shows whether the answer is right.

79644.q: In a number pyramid, you add two neighbouring numbers. At the bottom are 1, 1, 1 and 1. Which number is at the top?
79644.e: The second row is 2, 2, 2. The third row is 4, 4. At the top is 4 + 4 = 8.
79644.m: In a tall pyramid, the numbers grow quickly towards the top.

79645.q: In a number pyramid, you add two neighbouring numbers. At the bottom are 3, 3 and 3. Which number is at the top?
79645.e: The middle row is 6 and 6. At the top is 6 + 6 = 12.
79645.m: Equal numbers at the bottom give equal numbers in the next row.

79646.q: How many boxes does a number pyramid with 3 numbers in the bottom row have?
79646.e: There are 3 boxes at the bottom, 2 above them and 1 at the top. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
79646.m: Each row of a number pyramid has one box fewer than the row below.

79647.q: In a magic triangle, each side adds up to 10. One side has 5, 1 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79647.m: In a magic triangle, every side has the same sum.

79648.q: In a magic triangle, each side adds up to 9. One side has 1, 6 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79648.m: The missing number tops the side up to the magic sum.

79649.q: In a magic triangle, each side adds up to 12. One side has 6, 2 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79649.m: First add up, then top up to the sum.

79650.q: What is the same on all three sides of a magic triangle?
79650.e: In a magic triangle, the numbers on each side add up to the same number.
79650.m: All sides of a magic triangle have the same sum.

79651.q: A magic triangle has a box at each corner and a box in the middle of each side. How many boxes is that?
79651.e: There are 3 corners and 3 side middles. 3 + 3 = 6 boxes.
79651.m: A triangle has three corners and three sides.

79652.q: In a magic triangle, each side adds up to 11. One side has 4, 5 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79652.m: At the end, check every side by adding up.

79653.q: In a magic triangle, each side adds up to 20. One side has 10, 4 and a missing number. Which number is missing?
79653.m: Magic triangles also exist with bigger numbers.

79654.q: Why does a number in the corner of a magic triangle count for two sides?
79654.e: Two sides of the triangle meet at every corner. So the corner number belongs to both sides.
79654.m: In a magic triangle, a corner number belongs to two sides.

79655.q: How many matchsticks do you need for a square if each side is one matchstick?
79655.e: A square has 4 sides of equal length. You need one matchstick for each side.

79656.q: How many matchsticks do you need for a triangle if each side is one matchstick?
79656.e: A triangle has 3 sides. So you need 3 matchsticks.

79657.q: Two squares lie side by side and share one side. How many matchsticks do you need?
79657.e: Two separate squares need 8 sticks. The shared side is needed only once, so 8 − 1 = 7.
79657.m: Shared sides save sticks when you lay out matchsticks.

79658.q: Three squares lie in a row and share the sides between them. How many matchsticks do you need?
79658.e: The first square needs 4 sticks, each further one only 3. 4 + 3 + 3 = 10.
79658.m: Each extra square in the row needs only 3 more sticks.

79659.q: You have 12 matchsticks and use them to make separate squares that do not touch. How many squares can you make?
79659.e: Each separate square needs 4 sticks. 12 divided by 4 is 3.
79659.m: For separate squares, you divide the sticks by 4.

79660.q: How many matchsticks do you need to make the Roman numeral VI?
79660.e: The V is made of 2 sticks and the I of one stick. 2 + 1 = 3.
79660.m: You make the Roman five with two matchsticks.

79661.q: You make the Roman numeral IV with matchsticks. Now you move the I from the left to the right of the V. Which number do you get?
79661.e: If the I is to the right of the V, you add it. So IV becomes VI, which means 4 becomes 6.
79661.m: In Roman numerals, the position of a stick changes the value.

79662.q: How many matchsticks do you need for a rectangle with 2 sticks on each long side and 1 stick on each short side?
79662.e: The two long sides need 2 + 2 = 4 sticks, the two short sides 1 + 1 = 2 sticks. That makes 6 altogether.
79662.m: For the perimeter, you add up all the sides.

79663.q: How many matchsticks do you need for a hexagon if each side is one matchstick?
79663.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. You need one matchstick for each side.
79663.m: A hexagon has six sides and six corners.

79664.q: A pair of scales is balanced. On the left is 1 apple, on the right are 3 nuts. How many nuts weigh as much as 2 apples?
79664.e: One apple weighs as much as 3 nuts. Two apples weigh as much as 3 + 3 = 6 nuts.
79664.m: Whatever you double on one side, you must double on the other too.

79665.q: A pair of scales is balanced. On the left are 2 identical cubes, on the right is a 10-gram weight. How heavy is one cube?
79665.e: Two cubes weigh 10 grams together. 10 divided by 2 is 5 grams.
79665.m: Things of equal weight share the total weight equally.

79666.q: On a pair of scales there are 4 kilograms on the left and 7 kilograms on the right. Which side goes down?
79666.e: The right side, with 7 kilograms, is heavier than the left side with 4 kilograms. The heavier side goes down.
79666.m: The heavier side of a pair of scales goes down.

79667.q: A pair of scales is balanced. On the left are 3 kilograms and a parcel, on the right are 8 kilograms. How heavy is the parcel?
79667.m: When the scales are balanced, both sides weigh the same.

79668.q: A pear weighs as much as 2 plums. A plum weighs as much as 3 cherries. How many cherries weigh as much as one pear?
79668.e: A pear weighs as much as 2 plums. That is 3 + 3 = 6 cherries.
79668.m: You can swap weights step by step.

79669.q: A pair of scales is balanced. There are the same number of apples on both sides. You take one apple away on the left. What happens?
79669.e: The left is now lighter. So the heavier right side goes down.
79669.m: If you take something away on one side, that side gets lighter.

79670.q: A pair of scales is balanced. On the left are 3 identical balls, on the right are 12 kilograms. How heavy is one ball?
79670.e: Three balls weigh 12 kilograms together. 12 divided by 3 is 4 kilograms.
79670.m: For identical things, you divide the total weight by how many there are.

79671.q: A pair of scales is balanced. On the left are 1 banana and 2 grams, on the right are 9 grams. How heavy is the banana in this puzzle?
79671.e: The banana and 2 grams together are 9 grams. 9 − 2 = 7 grams.
79671.m: If you take the same away from both sides, the scales stay balanced.

79672.q: What do you write in a box of a cross-number puzzle?
79672.e: A cross-number puzzle works like a crossword, but with numbers. Exactly one digit goes in each box.
79672.m: In a cross-number puzzle, each box holds one digit.

79673.q: How many boxes does the answer 125 need in a cross-number puzzle?
79673.e: The number 125 has three digits: 1, 2 and 5. Each digit gets a box.
79673.m: A three-digit number needs three boxes.

79674.q: In a cross-number puzzle, the clue across is “6 + 7”. Which digit goes in the first box?
79674.m: With a two-digit answer, the tens digit comes first.

79675.q: In a cross-number puzzle, the clue down is “5 times 5”. Which digit goes in the bottom box?
79675.e: 5 times 5 = 25. Down answers are written from top to bottom, so the 5 goes at the bottom.
79675.m: Down answers are written from top to bottom.

79676.q: The answer across is 42. A down answer starts in the same first box. Which digit does it start with?
79676.e: The two numbers share the first box. That box holds the 4 of 42.
79676.m: Where two answers cross, the digit is the same.

79677.q: In a cross-number puzzle, the clue across is “100 − 1”. Which number goes in?
79677.e: 100 − 1 = 99. That is two boxes, each with a 9.

79678.q: In a cross-number puzzle, the clue down is “half of 30”. Which number goes in?

79679.q: The answer across is 36 and the answer down is 63. They share a box that is the second digit of 36 and the first digit of 63. Which digit is there?
79679.e: In 36, the second digit is 6. In 63, the first digit is also 6. So 6 fits.
79679.m: In the crossing box, both answers must have the same digit.

79680.q: What do you call a path in a maze that goes nowhere?
79680.e: A path with no way out is called a dead end. There you have to turn back.
79680.m: At a dead end you have to turn back.

79681.q: What is another name for a labyrinth with lots of branches and dead ends, where you can get lost?
79681.e: A labyrinth with branches and dead ends, where you can get lost, is also called a maze.
79681.m: You can get lost in a maze.

79682.q: Which rule often helps you get out of a simple maze?
a: Always keep one hand on the wall
79682.e: If you always keep the same hand on the wall, you will get out of a simple maze. This is called the hand-on-the-wall rule.
79682.m: With your hand on the wall, you can find your way out of simple mazes.

79683.q: You are facing north and turn right twice. Which way are you facing now?
79683.e: One right turn takes you from north to east, the second from east to south.
79683.m: Two right turns make a half turn.

79684.q: In a maze you are on square 5 of a row. You go 3 squares forward and 1 square back. Which square are you on?
79684.m: Going forward you add, going back you subtract.

79685.q: In the Greek legend, who helped Theseus out of the labyrinth with a thread?
79685.e: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread. With the thread he found his way back out of the labyrinth.
79685.m: Ariadne’s thread showed Theseus the way back.

79686.q: In which kind of field is a big maze often made in summer, because the plants are taller than children?
79686.e: In summer, maize grows much taller than a child. Paths are cut into it and you cannot see over the top. That is how a maize maze is made.
79686.m: A maize maze is made in a tall maize field.

79687.q: In a maze you go left and come to a wall. Which way do you turn to go back?
79687.e: To go back the same way, you turn all the way round. Then you walk in the opposite direction.
79687.m: To go back, you turn round.

79688.m: To cross ten, you add in two steps.

79689.q: Which statement about shapes is false?
79689.e: A triangle has only 3 corners. So the statement with 4 corners is false.
79689.m: A triangle has three corners and three sides.

79690.q: Which statement about the week is true?
79690.e: From Monday to Sunday there are 7 days. That is one week.

79691.q: Which comparison of 10 and 8 is true?
79691.e: On the number line, 10 is further to the right than 8. So 10 is greater.
79691.m: The further right on the number line, the greater the number.

79692.q: Which statement about even numbers is false?
79692.e: You cannot split 9 into two equal whole halves. So 9 is odd and the statement is false.

79693.m: Multiplying is adding the same number several times.

79694.q: Which statement about money is false?
79694.e: 1 franc has 100 centimes, not 10. So this statement is false.

79695.q: Which statement about half of 20 is true?
79695.m: Two halves make the whole again.

79696.q: A combination lock has 3 wheels. The code is 200 + 30 + 4. What is it?
79696.e: 2 hundreds, 3 tens and 4 ones make the number 234.
79696.m: In three-digit numbers, the hundreds come first.

79697.q: A combination lock has 3 wheels showing three identical digits. Added together they make 6. What is the code?
79697.e: Three identical digits make 6 if each digit is 2: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. The code is 222.
79697.m: Three equal numbers added together can also be worked out by multiplying.

79698.q: The code of a combination lock uses the digits 1, 2 and 3, from largest to smallest. What is it?
79698.e: The largest digit is 3, then comes 2, then 1. The code is 321.
79698.m: Descending means from large to small.

79699.q: A combination lock has one wheel with the digits 0 to 9. How many different codes are there?
79699.e: The digits 0, 1, 2 up to 9 make 10 digits altogether. Each digit is a possible code.
79699.m: There are ten digits from 0 to 9.

79700.q: A combination lock has one wheel. The code is 4 times 2. Which digit do you set?

79701.q: A combination lock shows 0 4 7. You turn the last wheel up by 1. What does the lock show now?
79701.e: Only the last digit changes: 7 becomes 8. The lock shows 048.
79701.m: If you turn one wheel, only that digit changes.

79702.q: A combination lock has 2 wheels. The code is a number whose two digits are both 5. What is it?
79702.e: Both wheels show a 5. Together that gives the code 55.

79703.q: The code of a combination lock is the number straight after 99. What is it?
79703.e: After 99 comes 100. Here a two-digit number becomes a three-digit number.

79705.e: 6 + 4 = 10. The number you are looking for is 6.
79705.m: What you add to 4 to make 10 is the answer.

79706.e: 15 − 6 = 9. If you work out 9 + 6, you get back to 15.
79706.m: You can check subtraction sums with addition.

79707.m: The inverse sum helps you fill the gap.

79708.q: Which number is missing in 3 times __ = 15?
79708.e: 3 times 5 = 15. The number you are looking for is 5.
79708.m: Every multiplication has a matching division.

79709.m: You calculate with tens just like with ones.

79710.q: Which number is missing in __ times 2 = 18?

79711.e: If you add nothing to 7, you still have 7. So the 0 goes in the gap.
79711.m: Adding zero does not change a number.

79712.q: In a number wall, the bottom bricks are 8 and 9. Which number goes in the brick above?
79712.e: 8 + 9 = 17. That goes in the brick above.
79712.m: Number walls are good practice for adding.

79713.q: A 3-by-3 block of a sudoku is missing only one number. It already contains 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9. Which number is missing?
79713.e: Every block needs the numbers 1 to 9 exactly once. Of these, only the 6 is missing.
79713.m: In a sudoku, every small block also needs all the numbers from 1 to 9.

79714.m: If the gap is at the front, addition helps.

79715.q: Which six letters does the top row of letters on a Swiss keyboard start with?
79715.e: The Swiss keyboard is called a QWERTZ keyboard after its first letters. In America it is QWERTY, in France AZERTY.
79715.m: In Switzerland people type on a QWERTZ keyboard.

79716.q: Which key do you press to start a new line?
79716.e: The Enter key, also called the Return key, starts a new line in a text.
79716.m: The Enter key starts a new line.

79717.q: Which key do you use to delete the letter to the left of the blinking line?
79717.e: The Backspace key has an arrow pointing left. It deletes the character to the left of the blinking line.
79717.m: The Backspace key deletes to the left.

79718.q: What is the blinking line called that shows where the next letter will appear?
79718.e: The blinking line is called the cursor. The next character you type appears there.
79718.m: The cursor shows where you are writing.

79719.q: Which letters with dots does the Swiss keyboard have for German?
79719.e: The Swiss keyboard has its own keys for ä, ö and ü. There is no separate character for the German sharp S, because in Switzerland people write “ss”.
79719.m: The Swiss keyboard has keys for ä, ö and ü.

79720.q: What is the block on the right of many keyboards that only has numbers called?
79720.e: Many large keyboards have a number pad on the right. There the numbers are arranged as on a calculator.
79720.m: The number pad helps you type numbers quickly.

79721.q: Which keys do you use to move the cursor up, down, left and right?
79721.e: The four arrow keys point in four directions. You use them to move the cursor in the text.
79721.m: The arrow keys move the cursor.

79722.q: Which fingers do you put on the keys when touch typing?
79722.e: In touch typing you type with all ten fingers. That way you write faster and do not have to look at the keys as much.
79722.m: In touch typing, all your fingers type.

79723.q: Which key at the top left often cancels something on the computer?
79723.e: The Esc key is at the top left. “Esc” comes from the English word “escape”. You use it to leave full screen, for example.
79723.m: You often cancel something with the Esc key.

79724.q: Why is the computer mouse called a “mouse”?
a: The cable looks like a tail
It used to always be grey
79724.e: The first mice had a cable at the back. Their shape and size were like a small mouse, and the cable was like its tail.
79724.m: The mouse gets its name from its shape with the cable.

79725.q: Which mouse button do you usually click with?
79725.e: For normal clicks you use the left mouse button. The right button opens a small menu.
79725.m: Normally you click with the left mouse button.

79726.q: What does a click with the right mouse button usually open?
79726.e: The right mouse button opens a context menu. It lists things you can do with what you clicked on.
79726.m: The right mouse button opens a menu.

79727.q: What is the little wheel between the mouse buttons for?
79727.e: If you turn the mouse wheel, the page on the screen moves up or down. This is called scrolling.
79727.m: With the mouse wheel you scroll through a page.

79728.q: What do you call moving a picture to another place while holding down the mouse button?
79728.e: You click on something, hold the button down, pull it away and let go. This is called drag and drop.
79728.m: When you drag and drop, you hold the mouse button down.

79729.q: What do you often put the mouse on so that it glides well?
79729.e: A mouse mat is a flat surface. The mouse glides well on it and the sensor detects the movement reliably.
79729.m: A mouse mat is the surface for the mouse.

79730.q: What does a laptop often have instead of a mouse?
79730.e: A touchpad is a smooth surface below the keyboard. When you move your finger on it, the pointer moves.
79730.m: On a laptop, the touchpad often replaces the mouse.

79731.q: What do you need for a wireless mouse without a cable?
79731.e: A wireless mouse has no cable and so gets no power from the computer. It needs batteries or a rechargeable battery.
79731.m: A mouse without a cable needs its own power source.

79732.q: What happens to the mouse pointer when you push the mouse to the right?
79732.e: The pointer follows the movement of the mouse. If you push the mouse to the right, the pointer moves to the right too.
79732.m: The mouse pointer moves like the mouse.

79733.q: What is another word for a computer screen?
79733.e: A computer's screen is also called a monitor.
79733.m: A monitor is a computer screen.

79734.q: What is the area with the little pictures that you see after starting the computer called?
79734.e: The desktop is the work area on the screen. Small pictures for programs and folders are on it.
79734.m: The desktop is the computer's work area.

79735.q: What is the picture you see in the background of the desktop called?
79735.e: The picture behind all the windows and icons is called the wallpaper. You can choose it yourself.
79735.m: You can choose the wallpaper yourself.

79736.q: Roughly how far should your eyes be from the screen?
79736.e: Experts recommend a distance of about an arm's length from the screen. This is easier on the eyes.
79736.m: Keep about an arm's length away from the screen.

79737.q: What is good for your eyes when you look at a screen for a long time?
a: Taking breaks and looking into the distance
79737.e: Breaks and looking into the distance relax the eyes. Looking at the screen for a long time without a break makes your eyes tired.
79737.m: Short breaks are good for your eyes.

79738.q: What is the best thing to clean a screen with?
79738.e: A soft, dry or slightly damp cloth cleans the screen without scratches. Too much water can damage the device.
79738.m: A soft cloth protects the screen.

79739.q: What is the setting called that makes a screen lighter or darker?
79739.e: With brightness you set how strongly the screen shines.
79739.m: Brightness makes the screen lighter or darker.

79740.q: What is the picture called that appears when the computer has not been used for a while?
79740.e: If the computer is not used for some time, it often shows a screen saver or turns the screen dark.
79740.m: The screen saver appears during a break.

79741.q: What is the small camera at the top of the screen for video calls called?
79741.e: A webcam is a small camera on or in the screen. It lets people see you during video calls.
79741.m: The webcam lets people see you in video calls.

79742.q: Which printer prints with tiny drops of ink?
79742.e: An inkjet printer sprays tiny drops of ink onto the paper.
79742.m: The inkjet printer prints with ink.

79743.q: What does an inkjet printer need when the ink runs out?
79743.e: The ink is in cartridges. When a cartridge is empty, you put in a new one.
79743.m: Empty ink cartridges have to be replaced.

79744.q: What is the fine colour powder a laser printer prints with called?
79744.e: A laser printer uses a fine colour powder. It is called toner and is fixed onto the paper with heat.
79744.m: A laser printer prints with toner.

79745.q: Which printer can make real objects out of plastic?
79745.e: A 3D printer builds objects layer by layer, often from melted plastic.

79746.q: What does the print preview show?
a: What the sheet will look like
79746.e: In the print preview you see before printing what the page will look like on paper. That way you save paper.
79746.m: The print preview shows the sheet before printing.

79747.q: What is the device called that reads a sheet of paper into the computer?
79747.e: A scanner makes a picture of a sheet and sends it to the computer. The printer does the opposite.
79747.m: The scanner reads paper into the computer.

79748.q: How do you save paper when printing?
79748.e: If you only print what you really need, you save paper, ink and electricity.
79748.m: Only print what you really need.

79749.q: What happens with a paper jam in the printer?
79749.e: In a paper jam, a sheet gets stuck in the printer. Then you have to pull it out carefully.
79749.m: In a paper jam, a sheet is stuck.

79750.q: What do you use headphones on the computer for?
a: To hear sounds on your own
79750.e: With headphones you hear sounds right at your ear. That way you do not disturb other people.
79750.m: With headphones you can listen without disturbing others.

79751.q: Why should you not listen too loudly with headphones?
79751.e: Very loud sounds right at the ear can damage your hearing over time. That is why you set the volume pleasantly low.
79751.m: Music that is too loud harms your ears.

79752.q: What are headphones with a built-in microphone called?
79752.e: A headset is headphones with a microphone. With it you can listen and speak, for example in a video call.
79752.m: A headset comes with a microphone.

79753.q: What are very small headphones that you put straight into your ear called?
79753.e: Small headphones that go in the ear are called earphones or in-ear headphones.
79753.m: You put earphones into your ear.

79754.q: Which wireless technology do many headphones use to connect without a cable?
79754.e: Many wireless headphones connect to the computer, tablet or mobile phone via Bluetooth.
79754.m: Wireless headphones often connect via Bluetooth.

79755.q: What do L and R on the sides of headphones stand for?
79755.e: L stands for left and R for right. That way you put the headphones on correctly.
79755.m: On headphones, L stands for left and R for right.

79756.q: Why should you not wear loud headphones in traffic?
a: You cannot hear cars and bikes
79756.e: With loud music in your ears, you hear cars, bikes or warning signals badly. That is dangerous.
79756.m: In traffic you must be able to hear well.

79757.q: Where do you plug headphones with a cable into the computer?
79757.e: Headphones with a cable have a small plug. It goes into the headphone socket on the computer or screen.
79757.m: Headphones with a cable plug into the headphone socket.

79758.q: What do you do when you double-click?
a: Press once for a long time
79758.e: When you double-click, you press the left mouse button twice briefly, one right after the other.
79758.m: A double-click is two quick clicks.

79759.q: What usually happens when you double-click a program icon?
79759.e: A double-click on an icon usually opens the program, file or folder.
79759.m: You open something with a double-click.

79760.q: Where can you set how fast a double-click has to be?
79760.e: In the mouse settings you can change the double-click speed. Then it also works with slower clicks.
79760.m: You set the double-click speed in the mouse settings.

79761.q: What happens if the two clicks are too slow?
a: It does not count as a double-click
79761.e: If the two clicks are too far apart, the computer sees two single clicks. Then nothing opens.
79761.m: For a double-click you have to click quickly.

79762.q: What does a double-click on a folder open?
79762.e: If you double-click a folder, you see what is saved in it.
79762.m: A double-click on a folder shows its contents.

79763.q: What does a single click on an icon usually do?
79763.e: A single click only selects the icon. Only a double-click opens it.

79764.q: What does a double-click on a word in a text often do?
79764.e: In many writing programs, a double-click selects a whole word.
79764.m: A double-click selects a whole word.

79765.q: How do you double-click on a touchpad?
79765.e: On the touchpad you tap twice quickly with your finger. That works like a double-click.
79765.m: On a touchpad you tap twice for a double-click.

79766.q: What is an icon on the computer?
79766.e: An icon is a small picture on the screen. It stands for a program, a file or a folder.
79766.m: An icon is a small picture for something on the computer.

79768.q: What does the print icon usually look like?
79768.e: The print icon usually shows a small printer. That way you recognise it without words.
79768.m: The picture shows what an icon does.

79769.q: What does an icon with a magnifying glass often stand for?
79769.e: You look closely with a magnifying glass. That is why the magnifying glass icon usually stands for searching.
79769.m: The magnifying glass icon stands for searching.

79770.q: What does an icon with a cog often stand for?
79770.e: The cog stands for technology. With this icon you usually open the settings.
79770.m: The cog icon opens the settings.

79771.q: What does an icon with a small house often stand for?
79771.e: The house icon usually takes you back to the home page, so back home.
79771.m: The house icon takes you to the home page.

79772.q: What does an icon with a loudspeaker often stand for?
79772.e: With the loudspeaker icon you set how loud the computer is.
79772.m: You set the volume with the loudspeaker icon.

79773.q: What does an icon with a floppy disk often stand for?
79773.e: In the past, people saved files on floppy disks. That is why the floppy disk icon still stands for saving today.
79773.m: The floppy disk icon stands for saving.

79774.q: How do you close a program window on Windows?
a: With the X at the top right
79774.e: At the top right of a window there is an X. Clicking on it closes the window.
79774.m: You close a window with the X.

79775.q: What is the top bar of a window with the name of the program called?
79775.e: Right at the top of the window, the title bar shows the name of the program or file.
79775.m: The title bar shows the name of the window.

79776.q: What does the button with the small line at the top right of a window do?
79776.e: The line minimises the window. It disappears from the screen but stays open.

79777.q: What happens if you maximise a window?
79777.e: Maximising means making it big. The window becomes as big as the whole screen.
79777.m: A maximised window is the size of the screen.

79778.q: How do you move a window to another place?
a: Drag it by the title bar
79778.e: You click on the title bar, hold the mouse button down and drag the window to the new place.
79778.m: You move windows by the title bar.

79779.q: What is the bar at the bottom of the Windows screen with the open programs called?
79779.e: At the bottom of the screen is the taskbar. There you can see which programs are open.
79779.m: In the taskbar you see the open programs.

79780.q: Can you have several program windows open at the same time?
a: Yes, lots at the same time
79780.e: A computer can have many windows open at once. They lie on top of each other like sheets of paper on a table.
79780.m: Many windows can be open on a computer.

79781.q: What is the bar at the edge of a window called that you use to move through a long text?
79781.e: With the scroll bar at the edge, you move the contents of a window up or down.
79781.m: The scroll bar shows more of the contents.

79782.q: Which window is active when several are open?
79782.e: The window you clicked on last is at the front and active. That is where what you type ends up.
79782.m: The window you clicked on is at the front.

79783.q: What do you need folders on the computer for?
79783.e: In folders you collect files that belong together. That way you find them again more quickly.
79783.m: Folders bring order to your files.

79784.q: What colour is the folder icon on Windows usually?
79784.e: On Windows, a folder usually looks like a yellow file folder.
79784.m: On Windows, folders are usually yellow.

79785.q: Which name does a new folder get first on Windows?
79785.e: When you create a folder, it is first called “New folder”. Then you can give it a name of your own.
79785.m: Give a new folder a suitable name.

79786.q: What do you call giving a folder a new name?
79786.e: Renaming a folder means giving it a different name.
79786.m: When renaming, a folder gets a new name.

79787.q: Which name is best for a folder with photos from ski camp?
79787.e: A good folder name says what is in it. You will find “Ski camp photos” again straight away later.
79787.m: A good folder name says what is in it.

79788.q: How do you move a file into a folder?
a: Drag it in with the mouse
79788.e: You drag the file onto the folder with the mouse button held down and let go. Then it is in the folder.
79788.m: You can drag files into folders with the mouse.

79789.q: What happens to the files if you delete a folder?
79789.e: If you delete a folder, you also delete everything in it. That is why you look inside first.
79789.m: When a folder goes, its contents go too.

79790.q: Where do you find a ready-made folder for pictures on many computers?
79790.e: Many computers already have ready-made folders such as “Pictures”, “Documents” or “Music”.
79790.m: Many computers already have a folder for pictures.

79791.q: Which key on the keyboard is the longest?
79791.e: The space bar is the long key right at the bottom in the middle. It is the longest key.
79791.m: The space bar is the longest key.

79792.q: What does the space bar do when you are writing?
79792.e: With the space bar you put a gap between two words.
79792.m: Between words you press the space bar.

79793.q: Which finger do you press the space bar with when touch typing?
79793.e: Your thumbs rest above the space bar. That is why you press it with a thumb.
79793.m: You press the space bar with your thumb.

79794.q: Where is the space bar on the keyboard?
a: At the bottom in the middle
79794.e: The space bar is in the bottom row in the middle. That way both thumbs can reach it.
79794.m: The space bar is at the bottom in the middle.

79795.q: What happens in many video programs when you press the space bar?
a: The video pauses or carries on
79795.e: In many video and music programs, the space bar switches back and forth between play and pause.
79795.m: In many videos, the space bar starts and stops.

79796.q: How many spaces do you normally put between two words?
79796.e: There is normally exactly one space between two words.
79796.m: There is one space between words.

79797.q: Which key do you press to jump in many computer games?
79797.e: In many games, the character jumps when you press the space bar. It is big and easy to hit.
79797.m: In many games you jump with the space bar.

79799.q: What do you press the Shift key for when writing?
79799.e: If you hold the Shift key down and type a letter, it is written as a capital.
79799.m: With the Shift key you write capitals.

79800.q: Which symbol is often on the Shift key?
79800.e: The Shift key usually shows a wide arrow pointing up.
79800.m: The Shift key shows an arrow pointing up.

79802.q: How many Shift keys does a normal keyboard have?
79802.e: A normal keyboard has one Shift key on the left and one on the right. That way you can write capitals with both hands.
79802.m: There is a Shift key on the left and on the right.

79803.q: Which character do you get on a Swiss keyboard with Shift and the key 1?
79803.e: On the Swiss keyboard, the plus sign is above the 1. With Shift and 1 you write +.
79803.m: The Shift key gives you the upper character on a key.

79804.q: Which key writes capitals all the time until you press it again?
79804.e: The Caps Lock key locks in place. Then you write all letters as capitals until you press it once more.
79804.m: The Caps Lock key writes capitals all the time.

79805.q: What do you have to do to write a capital A with the Shift key?
a: Hold it down and type A
Let go of it and wait
79805.e: You hold the Shift key down and type the A at the same time. Then you let go of both.
79805.m: You hold the Shift key down while typing.

79806.q: Which character do you get on a Swiss keyboard with Shift and the key 7?
79806.e: On the Swiss keyboard, the slash is above the 7. With Shift and 7 you write /.
79806.m: You reach many characters with the Shift key.

79807.q: How do you switch a computer off properly?
79807.e: When shutting down, the computer closes all programs properly and then switches itself off.
79807.m: You shut a computer down before it is off.

79808.q: Why should you not just pull out the plug?
79808.e: If you just pull out the plug, unsaved work can be lost. Files can also be damaged.
79808.m: Only pull out the plug after shutting down.

79809.q: What should you do before shutting down?
79809.e: Before shutting down, you save your work. That way it is still there next time.
79809.m: Save your work before shutting down.

79810.q: Where do you find the command for shutting down on Windows?
79810.e: On Windows you click on the Start menu and then on the power symbol. There you can shut down.
79810.m: On Windows you shut down through the Start menu.

79811.q: What does the power symbol usually look like?
a: A circle with a line at the top
79811.e: The power symbol is an open circle with a short line at the top. You find it on many devices.
79811.m: The circle with the line is the power symbol.

79812.q: What is it called when the computer goes off and comes straight back on?
79812.e: When restarting, the computer shuts down and starts again immediately. This often helps when something is not working properly.
79812.m: A restart often helps with small problems.

79813.q: What is the state called in which the computer sleeps but is quickly ready again?
79813.e: In sleep mode the computer uses only a little electricity. It wakes up again quickly.
79813.m: In sleep mode the computer is only asleep.

79814.q: Why do you shut the computer down in the evening?
79814.e: A computer that is switched off uses no electricity. This is good for the environment and your wallet.
79814.m: A computer that is switched off saves electricity.

79815.q: What does the fruit case of the horse chestnut look like before it bursts open?
79815.e: The shiny brown conkers first sit inside a green, spiky case. In autumn the case bursts open.
79815.m: The horse chestnut sits in a green, spiky case.

79816.q: Can you eat horse chestnuts like hot roasted chestnuts?
79816.e: Horse chestnuts taste bitter and are not edible for people. Roasted chestnuts come from a different tree, the sweet chestnut.
79816.m: Roasted chestnuts come from the sweet chestnut, not the horse chestnut.

79817.q: What does a horse chestnut leaf look like?
79817.e: A horse chestnut leaf is made of five to seven large leaflets. They spread out from one point like the fingers of a hand.
79817.m: The horse chestnut leaf looks like a hand.

79818.q: What do the upright white flower clusters of the horse chestnut look like?
79818.e: Lots of flowers grow together in an upright, pointed cluster. That is why people call them flower candles.
79818.m: In spring the horse chestnut has white flower candles.

79819.q: In which month does the horse chestnut usually flower?
79819.e: The horse chestnut flowers in late spring, usually in May. The fruits are only ripe in autumn.
79819.m: The horse chestnut flowers in May.

79820.q: When do ripe horse chestnuts fall from the tree?
79820.e: The fruits ripen in September and October. Then they fall down and you can collect them.
79820.m: You can collect conkers in autumn.

79821.q: Which animals like eating horse chestnuts?
79821.e: Wild animals such as deer and wild boar like eating horse chestnuts. That is why people often collect them as winter food for wild animals.
79821.m: Horse chestnuts are food for deer and wild boar.

79822.q: What do children often make from conkers and toothpicks?
79822.e: With toothpicks or matches you can join conkers together into little people and animals. It is a popular autumn craft.
79822.m: You can make funny figures from conkers.

79823.q: Which region does the horse chestnut originally come from?
79823.e: The horse chestnut grows wild in mountain forests in the Balkans, for example in Greece. Here it was planted in parks and avenues.
79823.m: The horse chestnut originally comes from the Balkans.

79824.q: What is the soft wood of the lime tree especially popular for?
79824.e: Lime wood is soft and pale and easy to work. Many wooden figures and nativity figures are carved from lime wood.
79824.m: Lime wood is good for carving.

79825.q: Why do bikes and cars under lime trees often get sticky in summer?
a: Aphids give off a sweet liquid
79825.e: Lots of aphids often live on lime leaves. They give off a sweet, sticky liquid that drips onto everything below.
79825.m: In summer sticky liquid from aphids drips from lime trees.

79826.q: Which insects love buzzing around lime trees in flower?
79826.e: Lime flowers smell strongly and have lots of sweet nectar. Bees collect it and make honey from it.
79826.m: Lime trees in flower are a feast for bees.

79827.q: In which season do lime trees flower?
79827.e: Lime trees flower in June and July. Then it smells sweet under the trees.
79827.m: Lime trees flower in June and July.

79828.q: What helps the fruit of the lime tree to glide through the air?
79828.e: The small lime nuts hang from a pale, flat leaf. As they fall, it spins like a propeller.
79828.m: The lime fruit flies away on a wing-like leaf.

79829.q: How does the famous German folk song go on: “At the well before the gate there stands a …”?
79829.e: The words were written by the poet Wilhelm Müller. Franz Schubert turned them into a song in 1827, which many people still sing today.
79829.m: In the song a linden tree stands by the well.

79830.q: In which Swiss city do people tell the legend of the Murten lime tree?
